text: Kindred of the Carpathians watch the princes of the Dragon order fight the Turk and each other.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Lodi dynasty
text: Bahlul Lodi takes the throne of Delhi.

title: Pirates of the Aegean
text: Corsairs make the Aegean islands unsafe as Byzantine power ends.

title: Edo castle
text: Ota Dokan builds a castle at Edo, the future Tokyo.

title: Moravia in the Bohemian wars
text: Catholic lords in Moravia fight George of Podebrady's Hussites.

title: Ficino translates Hermes
text: Marsilio Ficino translates the Hermetic writings for Cosimo de' Medici; the Order of Hermes is delighted and alarmed.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Guru Nanak born
text: The founder of the Sikh faith is born.

title: Venice seeks allies in Persia
text: Venetian envoys go to Uzun Hasan for help against the Ottomans.

title: The Platonic Academy
text: Ficino's circle at Careggi studies Plato and Hermes Trismegistus.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Trent blood libel
text: The Jews of Trent are tortured and killed after a child's death.

title: The Birth of Venus
text: Botticelli paints the Birth of Venus about this time.

title: The sweating sickness
text: A new and deadly fever kills thousands in London.

title: Pico's nine hundred theses
text: Pico della Mirandola offers to debate nine hundred theses, many from the Kabbalah; the pope condemns thirteen.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

links.title: The great schism and the Paladins

title: Baza
text: Castile takes Baza after a long siege.

title: The new disease and the blood
text: Kindred learn quickly which mortals carry the French disease, and which feeding grounds to avoid.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Last Supper
text: Leonardo finishes the Last Supper in Milan.

title: Zonchio
text: The Ottoman fleet beats Venice.

title: A backwater ruled from Canton
text: Hong Kong's villages fish and farm while Canton grows into a great port.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

links.title: The sleeping dragons of Hong Kong

title: Wittenberg university
text: Frederick the Wise founds a university at Wittenberg.

title: Ivan the Great dies
text: Ivan III dies having tripled the lands of Moscow.

title: Trithemius and Faust
text: The abbot Trithemius warns of a vagabond calling himself Faustus.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Agnadello
text: The French crush Venice's army.

title: Agrippa's occult philosophy
text: Cornelius Agrippa drafts the Three Books of Occult Philosophy.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Brethren in Moravia
text: The Unity of Brethren grow in Moravia despite the king's ban.

title: A quiet march
text: The Unity of Brethren keep their faith in Moravia; inquirers from Prague find them hard to catch.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Ibrahim Lodi
text: The last Lodi sultan takes Delhi.

title: Raphael dies
text: The painter dies in Rome; Toreador of the city call it a loss to the blood itself.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Lutherans in Bohemia
text: Lutheran preachers reach Bohemia and Moravia.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Zwingli's reform
text: Zurich adopts Zwingli's reform.

title: Paracelsus burns the old books
text: Paracelsus burns Avicenna's canon at Basel and lectures in German.

title: Paracelsus and the craftsmen
text: Paracelsus's chemistry splits the alchemists: some go to the Hermetics, some to the Order of Reason.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Prague castle rebuilt
text: Ferdinand I rebuilds Prague castle in the new style.

title: Kindred in the kingdom of God
text: Kindred in Munster find the prophets' kingdom an easy place to hunt and a hard one to hide in.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Kannauj
text: Sher Shah Suri drives Humayun out of India.

title: The Prague fire
text: A great fire burns Prague's Lesser Town and castle.

title: Sher Shah dies
text: Sher Shah Suri dies in a gunpowder explosion.

title: Altan Khan at Beijing
text: The Mongol Altan Khan burns the suburbs of Beijing.

title: Humayun returns
text: Humayun takes back Delhi.

title: The age of printing
text: Antwerp printers flood Europe with books; the Order of Reason backs the printers of almanacs.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Toreador and the wars of religion
text: The Grand Court's Kindred back Catholic and Huguenot nobles as it suits them.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

links.title: France in the Age of Masks

title: John Dee's Monad
text: John Dee publishes the Hieroglyphic Monad; the Hermetic houses of England court him.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Fatehpur Sikri
text: Akbar builds a new capital near Agra.

title: Nagasaki opened
text: Nagasaki is opened to Portuguese trade.

title: The house of worship
text: Akbar invites scholars of every faith to debate at his court.

title: Akbar's decree
text: Akbar claims the right to judge disputes of Islamic law.

title: Kindred at Rudolf's court
text: Rudolf's alchemists and astrologers draw Tremere and Toreador to Prague.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Dee and Kelley in Bohemia
text: John Dee and Edward Kelley come to Bohemia to speak with angels.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Trier witch trials
text: Hundreds are burned in the Trier trials over a decade.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Dietrich Flade burned
text: A judge who doubted the witch trials is himself burned at Trier.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Rudolf's cabinet of curiosities
text: Rudolf fills his rooms with clocks, stones, paintings and marvels.

title: Nicholas Remy's book
text: A witch judge of Lorraine publishes his book on demons, boasting of hundreds burned.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: King James's Daemonologie
text: James VI of Scotland writes against witches.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Tycho in Prague
text: Tycho Brahe becomes imperial mathematician to Rudolf.

title: The Great Law of Peace
text: By one tradition five nations of the Haudenosaunee bury their weapons under a white pine about this time and form a league.

title: Machu Picchu
text: Pachacuti has a royal estate built on a ridge above the Urubamba.

title: The famine of One Rabbit
text: Frost and drought starve the Valley of Mexico for years; families sell themselves for maize.

title: The Inca take Chimor
text: Tupac Inca Yupanqui conquers the Chimu kingdom and carries its king to Cuzco.

title: The Great Temple rededicated
text: Ahuitzotl rededicates the Great Temple with the sacrifice of thousands of captives over four days.

title: The second voyage
text: Seventeen ships bring settlers, horses, pigs and sickness to Hispaniola.

title: Santo Domingo
text: Bartholomew Columbus founds Santo Domingo, the oldest European city in the Americas still lived in.

title: Moctezuma the younger
text: Moctezuma Xocoyotzin becomes ruler of the Mexica at the height of their power.

title: The first enslaved Africans in the Americas
text: The new governor of Hispaniola brings enslaved Africans from Spain to the island.

title: Montesinos preaches
text: A Dominican friar tells the settlers of Hispaniola from the pulpit that they are in mortal sin for their cruelty to the Taino.

title: Balboa sees the Pacific
text: Balboa crosses the isthmus of Panama and wades into the South Sea to claim it for Castile.

title: Cortes lands
text: Hernan Cortes lands on the Gulf coast with some five hundred soldiers, marches inland and enters Tenochtitlan as a guest.

title: Smallpox and the Night of Sorrows
text: The Mexica drive the Spaniards out with great loss, and smallpox then kills a large part of the city.

title: Tenochtitlan falls
text: After a siege of three months Cortes and his Tlaxcalan allies take the ruined city.

title: The dead of the conquest
text: The house reading has the plagues and the siege fill the lands of the dead beyond anything their keepers can bear; the wraiths' books tell of a Dark Kingdom of the Americas broken in these years.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Huayna Capac dies
text: The Inca emperor dies of a sickness that runs ahead of the Spaniards, and two sons fight over the empire.

title: Our Lady of Guadalupe
text: By the church's account a Nahua convert sees the Virgin on the hill of Tepeyac outside Mexico City.

title: Cajamarca
text: Pizarro seizes the Inca Atahualpa in the square of Cajamarca and kills thousands of the escort.

title: Atahualpa killed
text: Atahualpa fills a room with gold for a ransom and is strangled anyway; the Spaniards take Cuzco.

title: Lima founded
text: Pizarro founds the City of the Kings near the coast.

title: Cartier on the Saint Lawrence
text: Jacques Cartier sails up the river to the Iroquoian town of Hochelaga, where Montreal will stand.

title: Coronado in the north
text: Coronado marches from Mexico to the Zuni towns and the plains in search of golden cities and finds none.

title: The New Laws
text: Charles V forbids the enslaving of the native peoples of the Indies; the settlers resist.

title: The great cocoliztli
text: A bleeding fever kills perhaps most of the native people of highland Mexico in three years.

title: The silver mountain
text: Silver is found at Potosi, and within a generation a city larger than Paris stands at four thousand metres.

title: Salvador da Bahia
text: The Portuguese crown founds Salvador as the capital of Brazil.

title: The burning at Mani
text: Friar Diego de Landa burns the Maya books and images of Yucatan.

title: Saint Augustine
text: The Spanish found Saint Augustine in Florida and kill the French Protestants settled nearby.

title: The Manila galleon
text: A ship finds the way back east across the Pacific, and for two and a half centuries a galleon carries silver to Manila and silk to Acapulco.

title: The Inquisition in the Indies
text: Tribunals of the Holy Office are set up in Lima and then in Mexico City.

title: The last Inca
text: The Spaniards take the mountain refuge of Vilcabamba and behead Tupac Amaru in the square of Cuzco.

title: The second cocoliztli
text: The bleeding fever returns to New Spain and kills about two million.

title: Roanoke
text: English settlers land on Roanoke Island off the Carolina coast.

title: The lost colony
text: A relief ship finds the settlement of Roanoke empty and the word CROATOAN cut into a post.

title: The Croatan
text: The house reading follows the Garou's own story: in these years the Croatan tribe gives itself whole to bind a great Wyrm spirit, and the Pure Ones are two tribes where there were three.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Huaynaputina
text: A volcano in southern Peru explodes; the ash darkens the sky, and the next years bring cold summers and famine as far as Russia.

title: The Cape Verde islands
text: Ships in Portuguese service find the empty islands of Cape Verde.

title: Sunni Ali
text: Sunni Ali takes the throne of Songhai and builds a fleet of war canoes on the Niger.

title: Sunni Ali takes Timbuktu
text: Songhai takes Timbuktu from the Tuareg, and many of its scholars are killed or flee.

title: The castle of Elmina
text: The Portuguese build a stone fort on the Gold Coast to trade for gold, and later for people.

title: The Portuguese reach Kongo
text: Diogo Cao anchors in the mouth of the Congo and sends envoys to the king.

title: The Cape rounded
text: Bartolomeu Dias rounds the southern tip of Africa in a storm.

title: The king of Kongo baptised
text: Nzinga a Nkuwu is baptised as Joao the First of Kongo.

title: Askia Muhammad
text: A general overthrows Sunni Ali's son and rules Songhai as Askia Muhammad, patron of the scholars of Timbuktu.

title: Vasco da Gama on the Swahili coast
text: The Portuguese fleet calls at Mozambique, Mombasa and Malindi, where it finds a pilot for India.

title: Kilwa and Mombasa sacked
text: A Portuguese fleet takes Kilwa and burns Mombasa.

title: Afonso of Kongo
text: Afonso the First wins the throne of Kongo and makes it a Christian kingdom with its own bishop and schools.

title: Leo Africanus in Timbuktu
text: A young envoy from Fez visits Timbuktu about this year and later writes that books sell there for more than any other goods.

title: Afonso's letter
text: The king of Kongo writes to the king of Portugal that slave traders are carrying off even nobles and asks that the trade be stopped.

title: Ahmad Gran
text: The imam Ahmad of Adal breaks the Ethiopian army with Ottoman firearms and overruns the highlands.

title: Wayna Daga
text: Ethiopian and Portuguese musketeers kill Ahmad Gran, and the invasion collapses.

title: Hawkins's voyage
text: John Hawkins carries captives from the Guinea coast to Hispaniola, the first English slaving voyage.

title: The Jaga in Kongo
text: Invaders from the east sack the capital of Kongo, and the king regains it only with Portuguese guns.

title: Idris Alooma
text: Idris Alooma becomes ruler of Bornu about this year and arms his horsemen with Turkish muskets.

title: Luanda founded
text: Paulo Dias de Novais founds Luanda, which will send more captives across the Atlantic than any other port.

title: Tondibi
text: A Moroccan army with firearms crosses the Sahara and destroys Songhai at Tondibi.

title: Fort Jesus
text: The Portuguese build Fort Jesus to hold Mombasa.

title: Ahmad Baba in chains
text: The Moroccans carry the scholar Ahmad Baba and his library from Timbuktu to Marrakesh.

title: A second line in Tonga
text: The Tu'i Tonga keeps the sacred office and hands the daily rule to a brother, the first Tu'i Ha'atakalaua.

title: Umi of Hawaii
text: By tradition the chief Umi-a-Liloa unites the island of Hawaii about this time.

title: The age of the pa
text: As land grows scarce the tribes of Aotearoa build terraced hill forts.

title: Magellan at Guam
text: After ninety-nine days on the Pacific the fleet reaches Guam; a quarrel over a boat ends with houses burned.

title: The Portuguese sight New Guinea
text: Jorge de Meneses winters on the north-west coast of New Guinea.

title: Mendana in the Solomons
text: A Spanish fleet from Peru finds the Solomon Islands and names them for the gold it hopes is there.

title: Mendana's second voyage
text: The Spaniards reach the Marquesas, kill about two hundred islanders and fail to found a colony at Santa Cruz.

title: Tycho dies
text: Tycho Brahe dies in Prague; Kepler inherits his observations.

title: Kinsale
text: The English break the Irish and Spanish at Kinsale.

title: The Russian famine
text: Three years of failed harvests kill perhaps a third of Russia.

title: The Dutch East India Company
text: The VOC is founded and sells shares to the public.

title: Elizabeth dies
text: James VI of Scotland becomes James I of England.

title: The Tokugawa shogunate
text: Tokugawa Ieyasu becomes shogun and rules from Edo.

title: Kabuki begins
text: Izumo no Okuni performs the first kabuki in Kyoto.

title: The Gunpowder Plot
text: Guy Fawkes is caught under Parliament with barrels of powder.

title: The False Dmitry
text: A pretender claiming to be Ivan's son takes Moscow.

title: Don Quixote
text: Cervantes publishes the first part of Don Quixote.

title: Akbar dies
text: Akbar dies at Agra after nearly fifty years; his son Jahangir takes the Mughal throne.

title: The Peace of Zsitvatorok
text: The Long Turkish War ends at Zsitvatorok; the emperor stops paying tribute and the border in Hungary holds.

title: The Flight of the Earls
text: The Gaelic lords of Ulster flee to the continent.

title: The telescope
text: A spectacle-maker asks for a patent on a looking glass that sees far.

title: The Letter of Majesty
text: Rudolf II grants the Bohemian estates freedom of worship, a promise the Habsburgs will break within twenty years.

title: Kepler's new astronomy
text: Kepler publishes the New Astronomy in Prague, showing that Mars moves in an ellipse.

title: The Moriscos expelled
text: Spain begins expelling the Moriscos, some three hundred thousand descendants of its Muslims, over five years.

title: Henry IV murdered
text: Ravaillac stabs the French king in his carriage.

title: The Poles in Moscow
text: A Polish army takes Moscow and a Polish prince is offered the Russian throne in the Time of Troubles.

title: The moons of Jupiter
text: Galileo publishes the moons of Jupiter; the Order of Reason calls it proof, the Celestial Chorus a trespass.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The King James Bible
text: The authorised English Bible is printed, and its language shapes English for centuries.

title: Rudolf deposed
text: Matthias forces his brother Rudolf to give up the Bohemian crown; Rudolf is left with his collections in the castle.

title: Rudolf II dies
text: Rudolf II dies in Prague; his court of alchemists and artists scatters and his treasures begin to drift away.

title: Minin and Pozharsky
text: A Russian militia drives the Poles out of Moscow.

title: The Pendle witches
text: Ten people are hanged as witches at Lancaster.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Romanovs
text: The assembly of the land chooses sixteen-year-old Michael Romanov as tsar, ending the Time of Troubles.

title: The Globe burns
text: A cannon shot during Henry VIII sets the Globe alight.

title: Christianity banned in Japan
text: The shogun orders all missionaries out of Japan and the churches pulled down; Japanese Christians go into hiding.

title: The last Estates-General
text: The French Estates meet for the last time until 1789.

title: Osaka falls
text: The Tokugawa storm Osaka castle and destroy the Toyotomi family; Japan has one master.

title: Shakespeare dies
text: Shakespeare and Cervantes die in the same spring.

title: Copernicus banned
text: The Church puts Copernicus's book on the Index until it is corrected, and warns Galileo not to teach it as truth.

title: The Later Jin
text: Nurhaci proclaims the Later Jin, the start of the Qing.

title: The defenestration of 1618
text: The emperor's regents are thrown from a window of Prague castle; the Thirty Years War begins.

title: The Bohemian revolt
text: The Bohemian estates raise an army, take over the government and send envoys to every Protestant prince.

title: The Winter King
text: The Bohemians choose Frederick of the Palatinate as king.

title: Batavia
text: The Dutch take Jakarta and name it Batavia.

title: White Mountain
text: The Bohemian army is routed outside Prague in an hour; the Winter King flees and Bohemia's independence ends for three centuries.

title: The Mayflower sails
text: English separatists sail on the Mayflower for America to worship as they choose.

title: The Old Town Square executions
text: Twenty-seven leaders of the revolt are executed in Prague.

title: The truce ends
text: The war between Spain and the Dutch resumes.

title: The Anabaptists expelled
text: The Hutterite communities are driven out of Moravia; many go to Hungary and Transylvania.

title: The Amboyna massacre
text: The Dutch torture and kill English traders on Ambon.

title: Shah Abbas takes Baghdad
text: Shah Abbas takes Baghdad from the Ottomans and holds it fifteen years.

title: Richelieu
text: Cardinal Richelieu becomes chief minister of France and sets about breaking the Huguenots and the Habsburgs.

title: Charles I
text: Charles I becomes king of England and soon quarrels with Parliament over money and religion.

title: Dessau Bridge
text: Wallenstein beats Mansfeld's Protestant army at the Dessau bridge on the Elbe.

title: The Renewed Land Ordinance
text: Bohemia becomes Catholic by law; Protestants must convert or leave.

title: La Rochelle
text: Richelieu besieges the Huguenot port; it starves into surrender.

title: Moravia made Catholic
text: The Renewed Land Ordinance comes to Moravia; Protestants must convert or leave, and many lords go into exile.

title: Comenius leaves
text: The teacher and bishop of the Unity of Brethren, Jan Amos Comenius, leaves for exile in Poland and never returns.

title: The Edict of Restitution
text: The emperor orders all church lands taken since 1552 given back; the Protestant princes are driven toward Sweden.

title: The Bamberg trials
text: The prince-bishop of Bamberg burns hundreds as witches.

title: Gustavus Adolphus lands
text: Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden lands in Pomerania and enters the war on the Protestant side.

title: The Milan plague
text: Plague kills perhaps half of Milan; the city hunts for anointers said to spread it with ointment.

title: The sack of Magdeburg
text: Tilly's army storms Magdeburg; twenty thousand die in the sack and fire, and the city is a byword for horror.

title: Breitenfeld
text: Gustavus Adolphus destroys Tilly's army at Breitenfeld and the road into southern Germany is open.

title: Mumtaz Mahal dies
text: Shah Jahan's wife dies; he begins the Taj Mahal.

title: Vesuvius erupts
text: Vesuvius erupts after centuries of quiet and kills several thousand people around Naples.

title: Lutzen
text: Gustavus Adolphus dies leading a cavalry charge in the fog at Lutzen, though the Swedes win the field.

title: Galileo's Dialogue
text: Galileo publishes his Dialogue on the two world systems.

title: Galileo tried
text: The Roman Inquisition forces Galileo to recant his teaching that the earth moves; he spends his last years under house arrest.

title: Wallenstein murdered
text: The emperor's general Wallenstein, suspected of treason, is killed by his own officers at Cheb.

title: Nordlingen
text: The Swedes and their allies are destroyed at Nordlingen; France prepares to enter the war openly.

title: The Peace of Prague
text: The emperor makes peace with Saxony and most Lutheran princes; the war goes on, now a contest of France and the Habsburgs.

title: The French Academy
text: Richelieu founds the Academie francaise to guard the French language.

title: The Qing
text: Hong Taiji renames his Later Jin state the Great Qing and his people the Manchu.

title: Descartes's Discourse
text: Descartes publishes the Discourse on Method: I think, therefore I am.

title: Tulip mania
text: The price of tulip bulbs in Holland collapses overnight, ruining speculators.

title: The Shimabara rising
text: Christian peasants of Shimabara and Amakusa rise against taxes and persecution in Kyushu.

title: Baghdad retaken
text: Sultan Murad IV takes Baghdad back from Persia and kills much of its garrison.

title: Hara castle
text: The Shimabara rebels are killed to the last.

title: Japan closed
text: Japan expels the Portuguese and closes its ports.

title: The Treaty of Zuhab
text: The Ottomans and Persia sign the Treaty of Zuhab, fixing a border that lasts nearly to modern times.

title: Portugal free
text: Portugal rises, crowns the Duke of Braganza and breaks from sixty years of Spanish rule.

title: The Reapers' War
text: The reapers of Catalonia kill the viceroy and rise against Madrid; the war lasts twelve years.

title: The Irish rising
text: Irish Catholics rise against English and Scottish settlers; thousands die and the tales grow in the telling.

title: The English Civil War
text: King and Parliament raise armies and fight at Edgehill; the English Civil War has begun.

title: The Swedes take Olomouc
text: Swedish troops take Olomouc and hold it as their base in Moravia until 1650.

title: Richelieu dies
text: Richelieu dies; Cardinal Mazarin takes his place at the young king's side.

title: Rocroi
text: The French destroy the famed Spanish infantry at Rocroi.

title: Louis XIV
text: The four-year-old Louis XIV becomes king of France, with his mother and Mazarin to rule for him.

title: The Ming fall
text: Li Zicheng takes Beijing; the last Ming emperor hangs himself.

title: The Qing take Beijing
text: Wu Sangui opens the pass; the Manchus take China.

title: Marston Moor
text: Cromwell's cavalry win the north for Parliament at Marston Moor.

title: Brno holds
text: The Swedes besiege Brno for months and fail; the town is honoured for it ever after.

title: Naseby
text: Parliament's New Model Army destroys the king's army.

title: The Yangzhou massacre
text: Qing troops kill much of the population of Yangzhou in ten days after it resists them.

title: The Witchfinder General
text: Matthew Hopkins hangs about a hundred people as witches in East Anglia.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The war for Crete
text: The Ottomans invade Venetian Crete; the war lasts a generation.

title: Masaniello
text: The fisherman Masaniello leads Naples against Spanish taxes.

title: The Peace of Westphalia
text: The Thirty Years War ends; the Dutch are free.

title: The Swedes at Prague
text: Swedish troops take Prague castle and loot Rudolf's collections.

title: Khmelnytsky
text: The Cossacks rise against Poland; tens of thousands of Jews are killed.

title: The Fronde
text: Paris rises against Mazarin and the court flees the city; the Fronde lasts five years.

title: Sultan Ibrahim deposed
text: The mad Sultan Ibrahim is deposed and strangled; his seven-year-old son takes the throne.

title: Charles I beheaded
text: Charles I is beheaded outside his own Banqueting House in Whitehall.

title: Drogheda
text: Cromwell's army storms Drogheda and kills the garrison and many townspeople.

title: The Ulozhenie
text: Russia's law code binds peasants to the land.

title: The Swedes leave Olomouc
text: The Swedish garrison marches out of Olomouc after eight years, leaving a ruined town.

title: Leviathan
text: Thomas Hobbes publishes Leviathan: without a strong sovereign, life is nasty, brutish and short.

title: Worcester
text: Cromwell beats Charles II, who escapes by hiding in an oak.

title: Patriarch Nikon
text: Patriarch Nikon's reforms of Russian worship split the church; the Old Believers refuse them.

title: The Anglo-Dutch War
text: England and the Dutch Republic go to war at sea over trade.

title: The Taj Mahal finished
text: The Taj Mahal is finished at Agra as Shah Jahan's tomb for his wife.

title: Lord Protector
text: Oliver Cromwell becomes Lord Protector of England, Scotland and Ireland.

title: Pereyaslav
text: At Pereyaslav the Cossacks of Ukraine swear loyalty to the tsar.

title: The Deluge
text: Sweden invades Poland; the years of war that follow are remembered as the Deluge.

title: The Naples plague
text: Plague kills perhaps half of Naples in a single summer.

title: The Koprulu viziers
text: Mehmed Koprulu becomes grand vizier and saves the empire.

title: Cromwell dies
text: Oliver Cromwell dies; his son cannot hold power.

title: Aurangzeb
text: Aurangzeb imprisons his father and takes the throne.

title: The Peace of the Pyrenees
text: France and Spain make peace at the Pyrenees; Louis XIV will marry the Spanish infanta.

title: The Restoration
text: Charles II returns to London and the monarchy is restored.

title: The Royal Society
text: The Royal Society is founded in London for the advancement of natural knowledge by experiment.

title: Louis rules himself
text: Mazarin dies and Louis XIV announces that he will rule without a chief minister.

title: Kangxi
text: The Kangxi emperor takes the Qing throne as a child; he will rule sixty-one years.

title: Koxinga takes Taiwan
text: The Ming loyalist Koxinga drives the Dutch from Taiwan.

title: The Tatar raid
text: Ottoman Tatars raid Moravia and carry off thousands.

title: Szentgotthard
text: Imperial and French troops beat an Ottoman army at Szentgotthard.

title: The Great Plague
text: Plague kills perhaps a hundred thousand Londoners, a quarter of the city.

title: Kindred of the plague city
text: Prince Mithras's Kindred hunt among the dying while the court flees to Oxford.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Great Fire
text: London burns for four days; Kindred lose havens in the City, and some say a few of them lit the fire.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Sabbatai Zevi
text: The messianic claimant Sabbatai Zevi converts to Islam before the sultan.

title: The raid on the Medway
text: The Dutch sail up the Medway and burn the English fleet at its moorings.

title: Candia falls
text: Venice gives up Candia and Crete to the Ottomans after twenty-one years of siege.

title: Stenka Razin
text: The Cossack Stenka Razin leads a great revolt along the Volga before being captured and quartered in Moscow.

title: The disaster year
text: France invades the Dutch Republic; the Dutch open the dikes.

title: The De Witt brothers lynched

text: The house reading has the Order of Hermes recruit from the Golden Dawn, and a few of its members Awaken.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Whitechapel murders
text: An unknown killer murders at least five women in Whitechapel, and the press calls the killer Jack the Ripper.

title: The Ripper and the Kindred
text: The house reading has London's Kindred fear a Masquerade breach in Whitechapel; the prince sends hounds after the killer.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The year of three emperors
text: Wilhelm I dies, Frederick III reigns ninety-nine days, and Wilhelm II takes the German throne.

title: A hunter's diary
text: The house reading has an Arcanum scholar keep notes on the Ripper that point away from the Kindred and toward a mortal doctor.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Mayerling
text: Crown Prince Rudolf of Austria and Mary Vetsera are found dead at the hunting lodge of Mayerling.

title: The Eiffel Tower
text: The tower is finished for the World's Fair, the tallest structure on earth.

title: The Meiji constitution
text: Japan becomes a constitutional monarchy with a parliament on the Prussian model.

title: The Russian flu
text: An influenza pandemic spreads by rail from Russia and kills about a million.

title: Bismarck dismissed
text: The young emperor drops the old chancellor.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
text: Oscar Wilde publishes the tale of a portrait that ages while its sitter does not.

title: The Imperial Rescript on Education
text: Japan's schools are bound to loyalty to the emperor.

title: The Jubilee Exhibition
text: Prague holds a great exhibition and builds the Petrin lookout tower and a funicular.

title: The Trans-Siberian Railway
text: Work begins on a railway across Siberia to the Pacific.

title: The Mino-Owari earthquake
text: A great earthquake in central Japan kills seven thousand.

title: The tobacco protest
text: Persians stop smoking when the shah sells the tobacco trade to a British company; the shah backs down.

title: Cholera in Hamburg
text: Unfiltered water spreads cholera through Hamburg and kills eight thousand, while Altona next door is spared.

title: A doctor's case
text: The house reading has a Brno doctor's notes on a patient with no pulse who walks at night; the Arcanum buys them.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Indian members
text: The Indian Councils Act lets Indians sit on the legislative councils.

title: The Corinth Canal
text: A canal cut through rock opens across the isthmus of Corinth.

title: The Omladina trial
text: Young Czech radicals are tried and jailed, and Prague is placed under emergency law.

title: Dvorak's New World
text: Dvorak writes his symphony From the New World far from home.

title: The Dreyfus affair
text: A Jewish army captain is falsely convicted of spying and sent to Devil's Island; France splits for twelve years.

title: The First Sino-Japanese War
text: Japan defeats China in Korea and at sea, and takes Taiwan.

title: The Hamidian massacres
text: The sultan's irregulars kill Armenians in eastern Anatolia; over two years perhaps two hundred thousand die.

title: The third plague
text: Bubonic plague reaches Hong Kong; Yersin finds its bacillus, and the disease spreads by ship to every continent.

title: The Celtic revival
text: The house reading has the fae of Brittany and Ireland feed on the poets of the Celtic revival, and the Dreaming grows brighter there.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The first films
text: The Lumiere brothers show moving pictures to a paying audience in a Paris cafe.

title: X-rays
text: Rontgen finds rays that pass through flesh and show the bones.

title: Wilde convicted
text: Oscar Wilde is sentenced to two years' hard labour for gross indecency.

title: The Czechoslavic Ethnographic Exhibition
text: Prague shows peasant life from every Czech land, Moravian Wallachia and Slovacko among them.

title: The queen of Korea killed
text: Japanese agents murder Queen Min in the palace at Seoul and burn the body.

title: The first modern Olympics
text: The Olympic Games return in Athens.

title: Radioactivity
text: Becquerel finds that uranium salts fog photographic plates in the dark.

title: The Sanriku tsunami
text: A tsunami strikes the coast of northern Japan and kills over twenty thousand.

title: Plague in Bombay
text: Plague reaches Bombay and kills millions across India over the next two decades.

title: The Akashic Brotherhood shut the doors
text: The house reading has the Akashics close Tibetan monasteries to Western seekers after Theosophists come asking.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Diamond Jubilee
text: Victoria celebrates sixty years with troops from every corner of the empire.

title: Dracula
text: Bram Stoker publishes Dracula: a Transylvanian count, his voyage to Whitby and the hunters who stop him.

title: The Tremere and Dracula
text: The house reading has the Tzimisce furious at the book, the Tremere amused, and every hunter in England reading it twice.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Technocracy named
text: The house reading follows Mage canon: the Order of Reason takes the name Technocratic Union at its 1897 convocation.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Zionist Congress
text: Herzl gathers the first Zionist Congress in Basel.

title: The Badeni language ordinance
text: Vienna orders officials in Bohemia and Moravia to know Czech; German riots force the minister out.

title: The great Assam earthquake
text: One of the strongest earthquakes recorded strikes Assam and Shillong.

title: The Thirty Days' War
text: Greece fights the Ottomans over Crete and loses in a month.

title: Empress Elisabeth killed
text: An anarchist stabs the empress of Austria with a file by the lake at Geneva.

title: The Hundred Days
text: The Guangxu emperor orders sweeping reforms; the empress dowager stops them and holds the emperor prisoner.

title: Omdurman
text: Kitchener's machine guns destroy the Mahdist army outside Omdurman.

title: The Kaiser in Jerusalem
text: Wilhelm II rides into Jerusalem through a gap cut in the wall.

title: Mucha's posters
text: Alfons Mucha of Ivancice, in Moravia, is the rage of Paris for his posters of Sarah Bernhardt.

title: The Hilsner affair
text: A Jewish vagrant is convicted of ritual murder at Polna; Masaryk defends Hilsner and is called a traitor.

title: The Boxers rise
text: The Society of Righteous and Harmonious Fists attacks missionaries and Chinese Christians in Shandong.

title: The Hague Conference
text: The powers agree rules of war and found a court of arbitration.

title: The Interpretation of Dreams
text: Freud publishes the book that founds psychoanalysis.

title: Dreams on the couch
text: The house reading has the Dreamspeakers and the fae both uneasy as Freud teaches the waking world to pick dreams apart.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Klimt's patrons
text: The house reading has the Toreador of Vienna patron the Secession painters while the Ventrue fund their critics.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The siege of the legations
text: The Boxers and Qing troops besiege the foreign legations in Beijing for fifty-five days until an eight-nation army arrives.

title: The Eight-Nation sack
text: The relief armies loot Beijing and punish the north China countryside; the court flees to Xi'an.

title: The Boxers and the Kuei-jin
text: The house reading has some Kuei-jin courts feed the Boxer fury against foreign Kindred, and pay when the foreign armies arrive.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Paris Exposition
text: Paris holds the century's greatest fair, with moving walkways and the first Metro line.

title: Mendel rediscovered
text: Three botanists find Mendel's forgotten paper from Brno within months of each other.

title: The Labour Party
text: Trade unions and socialists form a committee to send workers to Parliament.

title: Planck's quanta
text: Max Planck proposes that energy comes in small packets, and physics begins to change.

title: The Golden Dawn splits
text: The Golden Dawn tears itself apart over Mathers and Crowley, and rival temples form.

title: The paradigm comes home
text: The house reading has a Technocrat in Brno quietly delighted as Mendel's laws return; the Progenitors claim them.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Victoria dies
text: The queen dies at Osborne after sixty-three years, and Edward VII takes the throne.

title: The wireless crosses
text: Marconi receives a radio signal sent from Cornwall across the Atlantic.

title: The D'Arcy oil concession
text: Persia grants a British prospector the right to drill for oil across most of the country.

title: The Brno technical college
text: The Czech technical university opens in Brno.

title: The Anglo-Japanese Alliance
text: Britain ends its splendid isolation in an alliance with Japan.

title: The campanile falls
text: The bell tower of St Mark's in Venice collapses into a heap of rubble.

title: Siam modernises
text: King Chulalongkorn's reforms keep Siam independent between British and French empires.

title: The suffragettes
text: Emmeline Pankhurst founds the Women's Social and Political Union: deeds, not words.

title: The May coup
text: Officers murder King Alexander and Queen Draga of Serbia and throw their bodies from a window.

title: The Kishinev pogrom
text: A mob kills forty-nine Jews over two days in Bessarabia while police watch.

title: The Ilinden rising
text: Macedonian revolutionaries rise against the Ottomans and are crushed with village burnings.

title: Bolsheviks and Mensheviks
text: Russian socialists split at their London congress, and Lenin's faction calls itself the majority.

title: The Sons of Ether part
text: The house reading follows canon: the Electrodyne Engineers' break with the Technocracy hardens, and they will join the Traditions.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Russo-Japanese War
text: Japan attacks the Russian fleet at Port Arthur without warning and lays siege to the port.

title: The Entente Cordiale
text: Britain and France settle their colonial quarrels and draw together against Germany.

title: The Hejaz Railway
text: Work presses on the railway from Damascus to Medina, built for the hajj.

title: Bloody Sunday
text: Troops fire on workers marching to petition the tsar, and revolution spreads across Russia.

title: Tsushima
text: Japan destroys the Russian Baltic fleet after its voyage around the world.

title: Mukden
text: Over half a million men fight for three weeks outside Mukden, the largest battle the world has yet seen.

title: The Potemkin mutiny
text: Sailors on the battleship Potemkin mutiny over rotten meat and sail to Odessa.

title: The October Manifesto
text: The tsar promises a parliament and civil rights to end the general strike.

title: The miracle year
text: A patent clerk named Einstein publishes on light, atoms and special relativity in one year.

title: The Brno university riots
text: Germans and Czechs clash over a Czech university in Brno; a joiner, Frantisek Pavlik, is killed by troops on the steps of the House of Artists.

title: The Persian constitutional revolution
text: Merchants and clerics take sanctuary and force the shah to grant a parliament.

title: The Kangra earthquake
text: An earthquake in the Himalayan foothills kills twenty thousand.

title: Dreadnought
text: Britain launches an all big-gun battleship that makes every other warship obsolete.

title: The Courrieres mine disaster
text: A coal dust explosion in northern France kills over a thousand miners.

title: Vesuvius erupts
text: Vesuvius erupts, kills over a hundred, and sends Rome's Olympics to London.

title: The Persian parliament
text: The first Majlis meets in Tehran.

title: Bengal partitioned
text: Lord Curzon divides Bengal, and the boycott of British goods begins.

title: Universal male suffrage
text: Austria gives every man the vote for the Reichsrat, and Czech and socialist members flood in.

title: The Anglo-Russian Convention
text: Britain and Russia divide Persia into spheres and settle Afghanistan and Tibet.

title: Les Demoiselles d'Avignon
text: Picasso paints the canvas that opens the way to cubism.

title: The Tiflis bank robbery
text: Bolsheviks led by Kamo and organised by a young Stalin rob a bank convoy with bombs.

title: Bosnia annexed
text: Austria-Hungary annexes Bosnia and Herzegovina outright, and Serbia and Russia are humiliated.

title: The Young Turks
text: Ottoman officers in Macedonia force the sultan to bring back the constitution.

title: Tunguska
text: Something explodes over the Siberian forest and flattens eighty million trees.

title: Tunguska and the Umbra
text: The house reading has the blast felt across the Umbra; Garou of Siberia and Mages argue over whether it was a falling star or a failed working.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Messina earthquake
text: An earthquake and tsunami destroy Messina and Reggio and kill some eighty thousand.

title: Martial law in Prague
text: Riots between Czechs and Germans bring martial law to Prague during the emperor's jubilee.

title: Oil struck in Persia
text: D'Arcy's drillers strike oil at Masjed Soleyman, and the Anglo-Persian Oil Company follows.

title: Bleriot crosses
text: Louis Bleriot flies across the English Channel.

title: Abdulhamid deposed
text: A counter-coup fails and the Young Turks depose Sultan Abdulhamid II.

title: The Adana massacre
text: Mobs and soldiers kill some twenty thousand Armenians in Adana.

title: Messina's dead
text: The house reading has the Shadowlands of Messina flooded with the earthquake dead, and Spectres gather.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Edward VII dies
text: Edward VII dies and George V becomes king; nine kings ride in the funeral.

title: Korea annexed
text: Japan annexes Korea.

title: The Portuguese Republic
text: A revolution ends the monarchy in Portugal.

title: The Manchurian plague
text: Pneumonic plague kills sixty thousand in Manchuria until a Malayan doctor's masks and quarantines stop it.

title: Halley's comet
text: The earth passes through the comet's tail, and people buy comet pills against poison gas.

title: A priest's warning
text: The house reading has an Olomouc priest send the archbishop a report of a parish where the dead do not stay buried.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Xinhai Revolution
text: Army units rise at Wuchang, the provinces follow, and the Qing dynasty falls within months.

title: The Delhi durbar
text: George V and Queen Mary are crowned emperor and empress of India in Delhi, and the capital moves from Calcutta.

title: Italy invades Libya
text: Italy attacks the Ottoman provinces of Libya; aircraft drop bombs in war for the first time.

title: The Mona Lisa stolen
text: The Mona Lisa vanishes from the Louvre; it turns up two years later in Florence.

title: The Agadir crisis
text: A German gunboat at Agadir nearly brings war with France over Morocco.

title: The fires of Istanbul
text: Great fires burn thousands of wooden houses in Istanbul.

title: The Titanic sinks
text: The liner strikes an iceberg on its first voyage; over fifteen hundred die.

title: The First Balkan War
text: Serbia, Bulgaria, Greece and Montenegro drive the Ottomans almost out of Europe.

title: The Meiji emperor dies
text: The Meiji emperor dies and General Nogi and his wife follow in ritual suicide.

title: The last emperor abdicates
text: The six-year-old Puyi gives up the throne, and China becomes a republic.

title: The Stockholm Olympics
text: The Stockholm Games bring electric timing and a photo finish.

title: Expressionism in Brno
text: Brno's Czech and German artists hold rival shows, and the town's cafes argue about modern art.

title: Albania declares independence
text: Ismail Qemali proclaims an independent Albania at Vlore.

title: The Second Balkan War
text: Bulgaria attacks its allies over Macedonia and loses.

title: The Redl affair
text: Colonel Redl, chief of Austrian counter-intelligence, is found to be a Russian spy and shoots himself.

title: The Rite of Spring
text: Stravinsky's ballet starts a riot in the theatre.

title: Emily Davison at the Derby
text: A suffragette runs onto the course at the Derby and is killed by the king's horse.

title: Hitler and Stalin in Vienna
text: A failed painter and a Georgian revolutionary live in Vienna the same winter; Trotsky and Tito pass through too.

title: The Tremere at home
text: The house reading has the Tremere of Vienna advising the court; their chantry is among the oldest in the empire, and they sense the war coming.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Imperator
text: Germany launches the largest ship in the world.

title: The Dublin lockout
text: Employers lock out twenty thousand workers in Dublin for over seven months.

title: The raid on the Sublime Porte
text: Enver Pasha storms the government offices, the war minister is shot, and the Committee of Union and Progress takes power.

title: The Vitkovice works
text: The ironworks at Vitkovice by Ostrava become one of the great steel and coal works of the empire.

title: Pentex's forerunners
text: The house reading has Glass Walkers watching a German chemical firm whose board answers to something in the Wyrm's service.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Trail of Tears
text: Soldiers march the Cherokee west at bayonet point; about a quarter die on the way.

title: The war with Mexico
text: The United States goes to war with Mexico over Texas and takes half its territory in two years.

title: Gold in California
text: Gold is found on the American River days before California passes to the United States; the world rushes in.

title: The Fugitive Slave Act
text: Northern officials and bystanders are bound by law to help return people who have escaped from slavery.

title: John Brown's raid
text: An abolitionist seizes a federal armoury to arm the enslaved and is hanged for it.

title: Fort Sumter
text: Southern batteries fire on a federal fort, and four years of civil war begin.

title: The Dakota war
text: Starving Dakota rise along the Minnesota River; thirty-eight are hanged in one day, the largest execution in American history.

title: The fifth of May
text: A Mexican army beats a French one at Puebla; the French take Mexico City the next year and crown an Austrian archduke.

title: Emancipation and Gettysburg
text: Lincoln declares the enslaved of the rebel states free on New Year's Day, and in July the rebel invasion of the north is broken.

title: Sand Creek
text: Colorado volunteers kill some hundred and fifty Cheyenne and Arapaho, mostly women and children, camped under a flag of truce.

title: The war of the Triple Alliance
text: Paraguay goes to war with Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay and in six years loses most of its men.

title: Appomattox and Ford's Theatre
text: The main rebel army surrenders, the president is shot five days later, and slavery is ended by amendment at the end of the year.

title: Morant Bay
text: A protest by black Jamaicans is put down with hundreds of hangings, and Britain argues for years over the governor's guilt.

title: Canada
text: Four British colonies join as the Dominion of Canada.

title: Maximilian shot
text: The republic of Benito Juarez shoots the emperor the French left behind.

title: The golden spike
text: Rails laid largely by Chinese and Irish workers join the two coasts of the United States.

title: The Chicago fire
text: A fire burns for two days and leaves a third of Chicago homeless.

title: The Greasy Grass
text: Lakota, Cheyenne and Arapaho warriors destroy Custer's command on the Little Bighorn.

title: The War of the Pacific
text: Chile fights Peru and Bolivia for the nitrate desert, and Bolivia loses its coast.

title: The North-West rising
text: The Metis and their Cree allies rise on the Saskatchewan; Louis Riel is hanged for treason.

title: Geronimo surrenders
text: The last Apache band at war gives itself up and is sent to prison in Florida.

title: The Golden Law
text: Brazil, the last country in the Americas to keep slavery, abolishes it; the empire falls the next year.

title: Wounded Knee
text: Soldiers kill some three hundred Lakota, many of them Ghost Dancers, on Wounded Knee Creek.

title: The Ghost Dance
text: The house reading has the Pure Ones' Garou among the dancers, and the dead of the plains answer the dance in the Shadowlands though the living cannot see them.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Klondike
text: Gold is found on a creek in the Yukon, and a hundred thousand people set out for it.

title: Canudos
text: The Brazilian army destroys a holy man's settlement in the backlands and kills nearly all its people.

title: The war with Spain
text: An American battleship blows up in Havana harbour; within the year Spain loses Cuba, Puerto Rico and the Philippines.

title: The Galveston hurricane
text: A hurricane drowns at least six thousand people on the Texas coast.

title: Mont Pelee
text: A cloud of burning gas from the volcano kills nearly thirty thousand people in Saint-Pierre, Martinique, in minutes.

title: Panama
text: Panama breaks from Colombia with American warships offshore and grants the canal zone within weeks.

title: The San Francisco earthquake
text: An earthquake and three days of fire destroy most of San Francisco.

links.title: San Francisco in the Gold Rush

title: The Mexican Revolution
text: A call to arms against the old dictator Diaz begins ten years of civil war.

title: Zanzibar the capital
text: The sultan of Oman makes Zanzibar the seat of the realm.

title: Blood River
text: A Boer wagon fort beats off Dingane's regiments on the Ncome.

title: The republic of Liberia
text: The settlers of Liberia declare a republic.

title: Tewodros
text: A former bandit is crowned Tewodros the Second and sets out to reunite Ethiopia.

title: The smoke that thunders
text: David Livingstone is shown the great falls of the Zambezi and names them for the queen.

title: The cattle killing
text: A young prophetess tells the Xhosa to kill their cattle so that the ancestors will rise; tens of thousands starve.

title: Diamonds
text: A child finds a diamond near the Orange River, and the rush that follows remakes southern Africa.

title: Magdala
text: A British expedition storms Tewodros's mountain fortress to free hostages, and the emperor shoots himself.

title: Stanley finds Livingstone
text: A newspaper's correspondent finds the missing missionary on Lake Tanganyika.

title: The slave market closed
text: Under the guns of the British navy the sultan closes the slave market of Zanzibar; a cathedral is built on the site.

title: Kumasi burned
text: A British expedition burns the Asante capital.

title: Isandlwana
text: The Zulu army destroys a British column at Isandlwana; the kingdom is broken by the end of the year.

title: The Mahdi
text: A Sudanese holy man proclaims himself the Mahdi and raises the country against Egyptian rule.

title: The Congo Free State
text: The powers recognise the king of the Belgians as the private owner of the Congo; millions die in the rubber terror that follows.

title: The scramble
text: The house reading has every hidden power of Europe follow the flags into Africa and find the continent already held: by its own shapeshifters, its own undead and its own dead.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Gold on the Rand
text: The richest goldfield in the world is found on the Witwatersrand.

title: The Matabele war
text: A chartered company's column with machine guns takes the Ndebele capital.

title: Adwa
text: The army of Menelik the Second destroys an Italian army at Adwa, and Ethiopia stays free.

title: The shortest war
text: British ships shell the sultan's palace at Zanzibar; the war lasts under an hour.

title: Benin sacked
text: A British expedition burns Benin City and carries off thousands of its brasses and ivories.

title: The South African War
text: The Boer republics go to war with Britain; farms are burned and families held in camps, where tens of thousands die.

title: The war of the Golden Stool
text: A British governor demands to sit on the Golden Stool, and the queen mother Yaa Asantewaa leads the Asante to war.

title: The Herero and Nama
text: German troops drive the Herero into the desert and issue an order to destroy them; most of the Herero and half the Nama die.

title: Maji Maji
text: The peoples of southern German East Africa rise, trusting in a water that turns bullets aside; the famine made in reprisal kills far more than the fighting.

title: The Congo taken from the king
text: After an outcry over the rubber terror Belgium takes the Congo from Leopold.

title: The Union of South Africa
text: The four colonies join in a union ruled by its white minority.

title: A native national congress
text: Black leaders found the body that becomes the African National Congress.

title: The Treaty of Waitangi
text: Maori chiefs and the British crown sign a treaty whose two texts say different things.

title: Gold in Victoria
text: Gold is found in New South Wales and Victoria, and the population of the colonies trebles in ten years.

title: The Eureka stockade
text: Soldiers storm a stockade of gold diggers who had sworn by a flag of the Southern Cross.

title: War in Taranaki
text: A disputed land sale begins twelve years of war between the crown and Maori.

title: Burke and Wills
text: Two explorers cross Australia from south to north and starve on the way back beside a river where the Yandruwandha live well.

title: Blackbirding
text: Ships begin bringing Pacific islanders to Queensland's cane fields, many by trickery or force.

title: The Waikato invaded
text: An imperial army crosses into the lands of the Maori king, and millions of acres are confiscated.

title: Fiji ceded
text: Cakobau cedes Fiji to Britain; measles brought home from a state visit to Sydney kills about a third of the Fijians the next year.

title: Truganini dies
text: The woman the colonists call the last Tasmanian dies in Hobart; her people's descendants live on.

title: Ned Kelly hanged
text: The bushranger who fought the police in home-made armour is hanged in Melbourne.

title: New Guinea divided
text: Germany takes the north-east of New Guinea and Britain the south-east.

title: Votes for women
text: New Zealand is the first self-governing country where women vote for parliament.

title: The Hawaiian kingdom overthrown
text: Planters backed by American marines depose Queen Liliuokalani; the islands are annexed five years later.

title: Samoa divided
text: Germany and the United States divide Samoa between them.

title: The Commonwealth of Australia
text: Six colonies federate; among the first laws is one to keep the country white.

title: The South Pole
text: Roald Amundsen's party reaches the South Pole with dogs and skis.

title: Scott's last march
text: Robert Scott's party reaches the pole a month after Amundsen and dies on the way back.

title: Sarajevo
text: A Bosnian Serb student shoots Archduke Franz Ferdinand and his wife Sophie in Sarajevo after their driver takes a wrong turn.

title: Konopiste falls silent
text: The archduke's estate at Konopiste in Bohemia, with its rose garden and hunting trophies, is left without a master.

title: The ultimatum to Serbia
text: Austria-Hungary sends Serbia demands written to be refused, and declares war when they are not all met.

title: Belgrade shelled
text: Austrian monitors on the Danube shell Belgrade the night after war is declared.

title: Germany declares war
text: Germany declares war on Russia and then France, and the great powers mobilise millions by rail.

title: The forts of Liege
text: Belgium's forts at Liege hold the German advance for days until giant siege howitzers crush them.

title: Britain enters the war
text: Britain declares war when Germany invades Belgium, over a treaty the German chancellor calls a scrap of paper.

title: Moravia mobilises
text: The regiments of Brno, Olomouc, Kromeriz and Jihlava entrain for Galicia and Serbia amid flags and quiet dread.

title: The burning of Leuven
text: German troops burn the university library of Leuven and shoot civilians; the rape of Belgium becomes a byword.

title: Tannenberg
text: Hindenburg and Ludendorff encircle a Russian army in East Prussia; its general shoots himself.

title: The Battle of the Frontiers
text: French infantry in red trousers attack into Lorraine and the Ardennes and lose over a quarter of a million men in weeks.

title: Mons
text: The British Expeditionary Force meets the Germans at Mons and falls back; tales of the Angels of Mons follow.

title: The Angels of Mons
text: The house reading lets soldiers' tale of the Angels of Mons be a real working, though no Tradition will say whose.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Cer Mountain
text: Serbia beats the first Austrian invasion on Cer Mountain, the first Allied victory of the war.

title: Japan enters the war
text: Japan declares war on Germany and turns on its Pacific islands and its port of Tsingtao.

title: The Galician battles
text: Russia routs the Austro-Hungarian armies in Galicia and takes Lemberg; Austria loses four hundred thousand men in a month.

title: Heligoland Bight
text: British battlecruisers sink three German cruisers in the first sea fight of the war, near Heligoland.

title: The Marne
text: The French and British stop the Germans on the Marne, some reserves rushed out from Paris in taxis.

title: The first trenches
text: Both sides dig in on the Aisne, and the race to the sea begins.

title: The siege of Przemysl
text: The Russians besiege the great Austrian fortress of Przemysl in Galicia.

title: The Masurian Lakes
text: Germany drives a second Russian army out of East Prussia.

title: Three cruisers sunk
text: One German submarine sinks three British cruisers in an hour.

title: Antwerp falls
text: The Belgian army slips out of Antwerp, and the city surrenders.

title: First Ypres
text: German volunteer regiments of students attack at Ypres and are shot down in thousands.

title: The Ottomans join
text: Ottoman warships, two of them German, shell Russian Black Sea ports, and the empire enters the war.

title: The Yser flooded
text: Belgium opens the sluices at Nieuwpoort and floods the Yser plain to stop the Germans.

title: The Emden at Penang
text: The German raider Emden slips into Penang harbour and sinks a Russian cruiser before being hunted down.

title: Tsingtao falls

title: Afghanistan neutral
text: The Afghan emir keeps out of the war despite Ottoman and German pleading.

title: The Carpathian winter
text: Austria attacks through the Carpathian passes in winter to relieve Przemysl and loses six hundred thousand men to battle and frost.

title: The attack on Suez
text: An Ottoman force crosses Sinai and tries to cross the canal; it is beaten off.

title: Dogger Bank
text: British and German battlecruisers fight off the Dogger Bank; the Blucher sinks.

title: Gas at Bolimow
text: Germany fires gas shells at the Russians at Bolimow; the cold stops the gas from working.

title: Tabriz changes hands
text: Ottoman and Russian forces fight over Tabriz in neutral Persia.

title: The Dardanelles shelled

text: Mines sink three Allied battleships in the narrows in an afternoon, and the fleet withdraws.

title: Przemysl surrenders

title: Neuve Chapelle
text: The British break into the German line at Neuve Chapelle and cannot go further.

title: The Czech Mafia

title: Chlorine at Ypres

title: The Gallipoli landings

title: The Armenian deportations

title: The defence of Van
text: The Armenians of Van hold their quarter against Ottoman troops for a month until the Russians come.

title: The 28th regiment

title: Gorlice-Tarnow

title: The Lusitania sunk
text: A German submarine sinks the liner Lusitania off Ireland; nearly twelve hundred die.

title: Italy declares war
text: Italy joins the Allies on promises of Austrian land.

title: Second Ypres ends
text: Second Ypres ends with the salient smaller and poisoned.

title: The first Isonzo

title: Lemberg retaken
text: Austria takes back Lemberg.

title: Kramar arrested
text: The Czech politician Karel Kramar is arrested for treason and later sentenced to death; the sentence is commuted.

text: Masaryk in Geneva declares war on Austria on the five hundredth anniversary of Jan Hus's burning.

title: The second Isonzo
text: Italy attacks again on the Carso and loses forty thousand men.

title: Warsaw falls
text: The Germans take Warsaw as the Russians retreat, burning crops and driving civilians east.

title: Suvla Bay
text: A new British landing at Suvla Bay stalls on the beach.

title: The great retreat
text: Millions of refugees flee eastward ahead of the Russian armies through the summer.

title: Loos
text: Britain uses gas for the first time at Loos; the wind blows some of it back.

title: The Champagne offensive
text: France attacks in Champagne with huge losses for a few miles.

title: The Rovno offensive
text: Austria's autumn attack in Volhynia fails and costs it a quarter of a million men.

title: Serbia overrun
text: Germany, Austria and Bulgaria invade Serbia from three sides.

title: Edith Cavell shot
text: The Germans shoot the British nurse Edith Cavell for helping Allied soldiers escape.

title: The landing at Salonika
text: British and French troops land at Salonika in neutral Greece too late to save Serbia.

title: Ctesiphon
text: The British march on Baghdad is stopped at Ctesiphon, and the army falls back on Kut.

title: The retreat through Kosovo
text: Serbian civilians and soldiers stream across the Kosovo plain toward the mountains.

title: The Serbian retreat
text: The Serbian army and King Peter retreat through the Albanian mountains in winter; tens of thousands die.

title: The siege of Kut
text: The Ottomans surround the British at Kut.

title: Gallipoli evacuated
text: The Allies slip away from Gallipoli at night without losing a man, after eight months and half a million casualties.

title: The Assamites watch
text: The house reading has the Assamites of Anatolia refuse the sultan's holy war, while Ventrue in Istanbul profit from the deportations.

title: Old dead of Troy
text: The house reading has a Reborn in Cairo dream of Troy's old dead stirring under the guns at Gallipoli.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Arcanum's war
text: The house reading has the Arcanum in London lend scholars to naval intelligence and lose track of half its own members.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Twenty-One Demands
text: Japan demands control over much of China, and Chinese students boycott Japanese goods.

title: The Singapore mutiny
text: Indian troops in Singapore mutiny and kill Europeans before they are put down.

title: Letters from Mecca
text: Sharif Hussein of Mecca and the British high commissioner in Cairo begin letters on an Arab rising.

title: The Lebanon famine
text: An Allied blockade, locusts and Ottoman requisitions starve Mount Lebanon; perhaps half the people die.

title: The Carpathian Garou
text: The house reading has the Shadow Lords of the Carpathians wage their own war, using the armies to drive rival septs from caerns.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Bread cards in Vienna
text: Bread is rationed in Vienna, and queues begin outside every bakery.

title: Arab nationalists hanged

title: Zeppelin raids
text: German airships bomb London and English towns by night.

title: Lights out in London
text: The house reading has London's Kindred find the blackout a gift for hunting, and the prince orders discretion.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Good Soldier Svejk is born
text: In Prague cells and barracks Jaroslav Hasek gathers the material for the soldier who survives by seeming a fool.

title: The Niedermayer mission
text: A German and Ottoman mission reaches Kabul to raise Afghanistan against India and fails.

title: Wassmuss in Persia
text: A German agent called Wassmuss raises the southern Persian tribes against Britain.

title: Bulgaria joins
text: Bulgaria joins the Central Powers.

title: The great storm at Gallipoli
text: A blizzard and floods kill soldiers in the trenches at Suvla.

title: Montenegro falls
text: Austria takes Mount Lovcen and Montenegro surrenders.

title: Erzurum
text: Yudenich's Russians storm the fortress of Erzurum in the winter snows.

title: The Serbs on Corfu
text: The survivors of the Serbian army are shipped to Corfu, where thousands die of disease on Vido island.

title: Verdun

ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Feeding at the front
text: The house reading has Kindred haunt the dressing stations behind Verdun, and the Camarilla struggles to stop Masquerade breaches among the dying.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The fifth Isonzo
text: Italy attacks again on the Isonzo with little gain.

title: Le Mort Homme
text: French and German troops fight for months over a hill called Dead Man.

title: The Easter Rising

title: The Rising and the Dreaming
text: The house reading has the Irish Kithain see the Rising as a poem made real, and the Unseelie mourn its poets.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Kut surrenders
text: The starving British at Kut surrender; many of the prisoners die on the march into Anatolia.

title: The Strafexpedition

title: Jutland
text: The British and German fleets meet off Jutland; Britain loses more ships but keeps command of the sea.

title: Sykes-Picot
text: Britain and France secretly agree how to divide the Ottoman Arab lands.

title: The Brusilov offensive
text: Brusilov breaks the Austrian line on a wide front, taking hundreds of thousands of prisoners.

title: The Arab Revolt
text: Sharif Hussein proclaims the Arab revolt against the Ottomans at Mecca.

title: Kitchener drowns

title: Phosgene at Verdun
text: Germany fires diphosgene shells at Verdun in its last push for Fort Souville.

text: The house reading has Black Spiral Dancers move freely in the Somme mud, and the Garou find the Wyrm grown fat on the battle.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Gorizia taken
text: Italy takes Gorizia in the sixth Isonzo battle.

title: Romania enters

title: Romani

title: Tanks at Flers

title: Romania driven back
text: German and Austrian armies drive the Romanians out of Transylvania.

title: The prime minister shot
text: Friedrich Adler shoots Austria's prime minister Sturgkh at dinner in a Vienna hotel.

title: Douaumont retaken
text: French troops take back Fort Douaumont.

title: Franz Joseph dies
text: The old emperor dies at Schonbrunn after sixty-eight years on the throne; young Karl succeeds.

title: The Tremere mourn an age
text: The house reading has Vienna's Tremere hold a vigil for the old emperor and begin preparing for an empire that may not last.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Somme ends
text: The Somme ends in mud and snow; over a million men are dead or wounded for six miles.

title: Bucharest taken
text: German troops enter Bucharest.

title: Rasputin killed
text: Russian aristocrats poison, shoot and drown the healer Rasputin.

title: Lloyd George
text: Lloyd George becomes Britain's prime minister.

title: The turnip winter
text: A failed potato crop and the blockade leave Germans eating turnips; hundreds of thousands die of hunger and cold.

title: The Brno hunger

ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Iteration X works

ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

text: The house reading has the Reborn of Egypt wary of Lawrence's band crossing old roads that hide old tombs.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

text: The house reading has a Moravian soldier home from Galicia tell an Olomouc priest of something that drank from the dead.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The February Revolution
text: Bread riots in Petrograd become revolution; the soldiers join the crowds and the tsar abdicates.

title: Baghdad taken
text: The British take Baghdad.

title: First Gaza
text: The British attack Gaza and fall back.

title: America enters

title: Vimy Ridge

title: Fatima

title: Zborov

title: Aqaba

title: The Corfu Declaration
text: Serbian and Yugoslav leaders agree to a kingdom of the South Slavs.

title: The Thessaloniki fire
text: A great fire destroys the old centre of Thessaloniki and its Jewish quarter.

title: China declares war
text: China declares war on Germany and sends labourers to France.

title: The eleventh Isonzo
text: Italy takes the Bainsizza plateau at terrible cost; Austria's army is near breaking.

title: Riga
text: Germany takes Riga with new infiltration tactics.

title: Sun Yat-sen in Canton
text: Sun Yat-sen sets up a rival government in Canton.

title: Caporetto
text: German and Austrian troops break the Italian front at Caporetto; Italy loses three hundred thousand men, most as prisoners.

title: Beersheba
text: Australian light horsemen charge and take the wells of Beersheba.

title: Third Gaza
text: The British break the Gaza line after taking Beersheba.

title: The October Revolution

title: The Piave holds
text: The Italians hold a new line on the Piave and Monte Grappa after the rout at Caporetto.

title: Jerusalem taken

title: The Russian armistice
text: Bolshevik Russia makes an armistice with Germany.

title: Kharkiv Soviet Ukraine

title: Ukraine's Central Rada
text: Ukraine's Central Rada declares autonomy, then independence.

title: Finland independent
text: Finland declares independence from Russia.

title: Hunger riots in Moravia

text: The house reading has an Egyptian Reborn serve as a labour officer with Allenby's army, looking for an old tomb in Palestine.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Olomouc's camps
text: Olomouc's barracks hold prisoners of war and the sick; typhus breaks out among them.

title: The patriarch restored
text: The Russian Church elects a patriarch for the first time in two centuries.

title: Gandhi at Champaran
text: Gandhi leads indigo farmers in Bihar in a peaceful campaign against their planters.

title: The mud of Passchendaele
text: The house reading has Glass Walkers find a Pentex forerunner selling the army gas masks that do not work.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Hunger and blood

ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The January strikes

title: The Epiphany Declaration

text: President Wilson's peace terms reach Vienna; they set out peace terms, among them self-determination for the peoples of Austria-Hungary.

title: The Kotor mutiny
text: Sailors of the Austrian fleet in the Bay of Kotor raise red flags; the mutiny is crushed and four are shot.

title: Kiev taken and lost
text: The Red Army takes Kiev and kills thousands; within weeks German troops drive them out.

title: The Treaty of Brest-Litovsk
text: Russia gives up Poland, the Baltic lands, Finland and Ukraine to make peace.

title: The Spring Offensive
text: Germany throws its armies from the east at the British in Picardy and gains forty miles in days.

title: The Paris gun
text: A German gun seventy-five miles away shells Paris; one shell kills eighty worshippers in a church on Good Friday.

title: The first flu wave
text: A mild influenza spreads through the crowded army camps in France, among them the great base at Etaples.

title: The Lys
text: Germany attacks again on the Lys; Haig orders his men to fight with their backs to the wall.

title: The Zeebrugge raid
text: The Royal Navy tries to block the submarine port at Zeebrugge with sunken ships.

title: The Red Baron shot down
text: Manfred von Richthofen is shot down and killed over the Somme.

title: The oath of the nation
text: Czech writers and deputies swear an oath in Prague to stand together until independence.

text: The Czechoslovak Legion, crossing Russia to sail home from Vladivostok, fights the Bolsheviks at Chelyabinsk and seizes the railway.

title: The Aisne offensive

title: Azerbaijan, Armenia and Georgia

title: The Piave

title: The Romanovs shot

title: The second Marne

title: The Czechs take Kazan
text: The Czech Legion takes Kazan and the Russian gold reserve.

title: Amiens

title: The second flu wave
text: A deadly strain of influenza breaks out in Brest, Freetown and Boston within weeks of each other.

title: Britain recognises the Czechs

title: Damascus taken

title: Karl's manifesto
