text: German sailors refuse a last sortie, raise the red flag at Kiel, and revolution spreads through Germany.

title: The Kaiser goes
text: A republic is proclaimed in Berlin, and Wilhelm II goes into exile in the Netherlands.

title: The Armistice
text: Germany signs the armistice in a railway carriage at Compiegne; the guns stop at eleven on 11 November.

title: Karl steps aside
text: Emperor Karl gives up his share of power in Austria; German Austria is proclaimed a republic.

title: Poland reborn
text: Pilsudski takes command in Warsaw, and Poland returns after a hundred and twenty-three years.

title: Masaryk president
text: The new National Assembly elects Masaryk president of Czechoslovakia.

title: The armistice of the dead
text: The house reading has the Shadowlands of the Western Front left crowded with ghosts who do not believe it is over.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Counting the cost
text: The house reading has the European septs count their losses after four years, and find that some caerns have gone silent.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Revolution in Munich
text: Kurt Eisner proclaims a Bavarian republic, and the Wittelsbach king flees.

title: Allied fleets at Istanbul
text: Allied warships anchor off Istanbul, and the occupation of the Ottoman capital begins.

title: The last shots
text: Soldiers die in the last minutes before eleven o'clock; the Canadians end the war where the British began it, at Mons.

title: The Hungarian Republic
text: Hungary is proclaimed a republic.

title: The Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes
text: Prince Alexander proclaims the united South Slav kingdom.

title: The Sudeten provinces
text: Czechoslovak troops occupy Opava and the German districts of Silesia and northern Moravia.

title: Slovakia secured
text: Czechoslovak and Italian-led troops push Hungarian forces out of Slovakia.

title: Slovakia joined
text: Czechoslovak troops close on Bratislava, then called Pressburg, and march in on the first day of the new year.

title: The Polish-Ukrainian war
text: Poles and Ukrainians fight for Lviv after the empire falls.

title: The Spartacists
text: The Spartacist League founds the German Communist Party; the January rising comes weeks later.

title: The influenza dead
text: The house reading has the influenza fill the Shadowlands with the young; the Hierarchy blames Spectres, and Heretic cults grow.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Tainted vessels
text: The house reading has the Kindred of London fall ill after feeding on the sick; the house rule calls it a taint of the blood, not a true plague.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The flu in India
text: Influenza kills perhaps twelve million in India, more than anywhere else.

title: The rice riots
text: Rice prices double and riots spread across Japan; the government falls.

title: The Persian famine
text: Armies, drought and influenza kill a large part of Persia's people.

title: The Russian Civil War
text: Red and White armies fight across Russia; the Czech Legion holds the Trans-Siberian Railway.

title: The Finnish Civil War
text: Reds and Whites fight in Finland, and the Whites win with German help.

title: The Legion's long road
text: The house reading has a Czech Hermetic in the Legion carry a talisman across Siberia, and Russian Traditions hunt for it.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Strangers in Vladivostok
text: The house reading has the Kuei-jin of the coast watch Allied armies pour into Vladivostok and decide to wait them out.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: A Reborn rides north
text: The house reading has an Egyptian Reborn with the Arab armies search for a scroll hidden in Damascus.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Hunters at the peace
text: The house reading has the Arcanum send scholars to Paris, fearing that new borders will move old guarded sites.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The blockade continues
text: The Allied blockade of Germany continues after the armistice, and hunger kills many more.

title: The Hebrew University stone
text: Foundation stones for the Hebrew University are laid on Mount Scopus.

title: Kafka's sanatorium
text: Franz Kafka, ill with tuberculosis, writes in Prague and the countryside while the empire falls.

title: The mark slides
text: The German mark begins the fall that will turn into the great inflation.

title: Cholera in Baghdad
text: Cholera and influenza strike Baghdad in the first months of British rule.

title: Shanghai's war boom
text: Chinese mills in Shanghai grow rich as European goods vanish from Asian markets.

title: Klimt and Schiele die
text: Klimt dies of a stroke in February and Schiele of influenza in October.

title: The Kithain choose a duke
text: The house reading has the Kithain of Moravia meet in a Brno cafe to choose a duke for the new republic's lands.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Moravian Shadowlands
text: The house reading has the influenza and the war fill the Moravian Shadowlands; the local Hierarchy cannot ferry them all.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Ludlow
text: Militia fire on a tent camp of striking coal miners in Colorado and burn it; women and children die in a pit under a tent.

title: Veracruz occupied
text: American marines take the port of Veracruz in the middle of Mexico's revolution.

title: The Komagata Maru
text: A ship carrying several hundred Indian migrants is held in Vancouver harbour for two months and sent back.

title: The Panama Canal opens
text: The first ship passes through the canal in the week the war begins in Europe.

title: Coronel
text: A German squadron sinks two British cruisers off Chile and is itself destroyed off the Falkland Islands five weeks later.

title: Haiti occupied
text: American marines land in Haiti after its president is torn apart by a crowd, and stay nineteen years.

title: The Klan refounded
text: After a film glorifying the old Klan fills the cinemas, a new one is founded on a hilltop in Georgia.

links.title: Atlanta in the Fourth Great Maelstrom

title: Villa's raid
text: Pancho Villa's riders burn an American border town, and an army chases them through Chihuahua for a year without catching them.

title: Yrigoyen elected
text: Argentina's first election by secret and universal male vote brings the Radical leader to power.

title: Mexico's constitution
text: The revolution's constitution gives the nation the land and the oil and limits the church.

title: Puerto Ricans made citizens
text: An act of Congress makes Puerto Ricans citizens of the United States weeks before conscription begins.

title: America enters the war
text: The United States declares war on Germany.

title: The East St. Louis riots
text: White mobs kill dozens of black residents and burn their homes; ten thousand march in silence down Fifth Avenue.

title: Brazil at war
text: Brazil declares war on Germany after its ships are sunk, the only South American state to fight.

title: The Halifax explosion
text: A munitions ship blows up in Halifax harbour and kills about two thousand people.

title: The flu at Camp Funston
text: Soldiers at an army camp in Kansas fall ill with a new influenza, one of the first recorded outbreaks.

title: The university reform
text: Students in Cordoba, Argentina, occupy their university, and their demands spread across Latin America.

title: The flu in the Americas
text: Influenza kills twelve thousand in Philadelphia in a month and empties whole villages in Labrador and Alaska.

title: Nigeria joined
text: Britain joins its northern and southern protectorates into one Nigeria.

title: Togoland falls
text: British and French colonial troops take German Togoland in three weeks; a Gold Coast soldier fires the first British shot of the war.

title: The Boer rebellion
text: Boer officers who will not fight for Britain rise against the Union government and are put down.

title: Tanga
text: A small German colonial force beats off a British landing at Tanga in East Africa.

title: Chilembwe's rising
text: A Baptist minister leads a rising against forced labour and the war in Nyasaland and is shot.

title: South West Africa surrenders
text: The German colony surrenders to South African troops.

title: Kamerun falls
text: The last German garrison in Kamerun gives up, and Britain and France divide the colony.

title: Zewditu crowned
text: The nobles of Ethiopia depose the uncrowned emperor Iyasu for leaning toward Islam and crown Menelik's daughter, with Ras Tafari as regent.

title: The siege of Agadez
text: Tuareg fighters of the Sanusi order besiege the French garrison of Agadez for three months.

title: The Mendi
text: A troopship carrying the South African Native Labour Corps is rammed in fog and sinks with over six hundred men.

title: The carriers
text: Something near a million African porters carry the East African campaign on their heads, and about a hundred thousand die of hunger and disease.

title: The flu lands in Africa
text: A naval ship brings the deadly influenza to Freetown, and it travels the coast and the railways; some two million Africans die.

title: The last surrender
text: Lettow-Vorbeck's undefeated column surrenders in Northern Rhodesia two weeks after the armistice.

title: Samoa taken
text: New Zealand troops take German Samoa without a shot.

title: German New Guinea taken
text: Australian sailors and soldiers take the wireless station at Bita Paka and the German capital at Rabaul.

title: Japan in the islands
text: The Japanese navy takes Germany's islands north of the equator.

title: The Emden sunk
text: The Australian cruiser Sydney destroys the German raider Emden at the Cocos Islands.

title: The Endurance crushed
text: The ice of the Weddell Sea crushes Shackleton's ship, and its crew camps on the floes.

title: The prophet arrested
text: Armed police raid the mountain community of the Tuhoe prophet Rua Kenana and kill two of the people.

title: The rescue
text: Shackleton, having crossed eight hundred miles of ocean in a boat, brings a ship back for every one of the stranded crew.

title: Conscription refused
text: Australians vote down conscription for the war, and do so again the next year.

title: The flu in Samoa
text: A ship from Auckland lands the influenza at Apia, and about a fifth of Western Samoa's people die; American Samoa, kept closed, loses no one.

title: The Paris Peace Conference
text: The victors meet in Paris to redraw the map of Europe and the Middle East; the beaten are not invited.

title: The Spartacist rising
text: Freikorps veterans crush a communist rising in Berlin and murder Rosa Luxemburg and Karl Liebknecht.

title: The Seven Days' War
text: Czechoslovakia and Poland fight over the coal district of Cieszyn Silesia, beside Ostrava.

title: The Hungarian Soviet Republic
text: Bela Kun's communists take power in Hungary for a hundred and thirty-three days.

title: The March killings
text: Czech troops fire on Germans demonstrating for self-rule in the Sudeten towns; fifty-four die.

title: The Egyptian revolution
text: Egyptians rise against British rule when the nationalist Zaghlul is exiled.

title: The March First Movement
text: Koreans read a declaration of independence in Seoul; Japanese troops kill thousands across the country.

title: Amritsar
text: General Dyer's troops fire into an unarmed crowd in the Jallianwala Bagh and kill hundreds.

title: The May Fourth Movement
text: Beijing students march against the treaty giving Shandong to Japan, and a new Chinese culture is born.

title: The Greeks land at Smyrna
text: Greek troops land at Smyrna with Allied blessing, and the war for Anatolia begins.

title: Mustafa Kemal at Samsun
text: Mustafa Kemal lands at Samsun and begins organising Turkish resistance.

title: The Treaty of Versailles
text: Germany signs the treaty in the Hall of Mirrors, accepting guilt for the war and huge reparations.

title: Scapa Flow
text: The interned German fleet scuttles itself at Scapa Flow.

title: Saint-Germain
text: Austria signs away its empire and is forbidden to join Germany.

title: Masaryk University
text: Brno gets its Czech university at last, named for the president.

title: Great Brno
text: Brno absorbs twenty-three villages and suburbs and becomes the second city of the republic.

title: Brno's Kindred renamed
text: The house reading has Brno's Kindred court give itself Czech names for its offices, and the German-speaking elders take offence.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Third Afghan War
text: Afghanistan fights Britain for a month and wins control of its own foreign affairs.

title: The Weimar Republic
text: Germany's national assembly meets at Weimar and writes a democratic constitution.

title: Trianon
text: Hungary loses two thirds of its land, Slovakia among it, by the Treaty of Trianon.

title: The Miracle on the Vistula
text: Pilsudski's Poles turn the Red Army back before Warsaw and stop the revolution from marching west.

title: Sevres
text: The Ottoman sultan signs away most of Anatolia; the Turkish nationalists refuse it.

title: The Czechoslovak constitution
text: Czechoslovakia adopts a democratic constitution on the French model.

title: Faisal driven out
text: France defeats King Faisal's Syrian army at Maysalun and takes Damascus.

title: The Iraqi revolt
text: Iraq rises against British rule; the RAF bombs villages to end it.

title: The mandates
text: The Allies give Syria and Lebanon to France and Iraq and Palestine to Britain.

title: The Reborn and the new Egypt
text: The house reading has the Reborn watch Egypt's nationalists with hope, for a free Egypt guards its own dead.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Czechoslovak Hussite Church
text: Priests break from Rome to found a national Czechoslovak church.

title: Kronstadt
text: The sailors of Kronstadt rise against the Bolsheviks and are crushed.

title: The Volga famine
text: War and requisitions bring famine to the Volga; five million die.

title: The Cairo Conference
text: Churchill makes Faisal king of Iraq and Abdullah emir of Transjordan.

title: The Chinese Communist Party
text: A dozen delegates found the Chinese Communist Party in Shanghai.

title: The Anglo-Irish Treaty
text: The Irish Free State is born, and the civil war follows.

title: The Order in Vienna
text: The house reading has Vienna's Hermetics salvage the old court library's secret shelves as the empire's archives are split.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Smyrna burns
text: The Turkish army retakes Smyrna, and the Greek and Armenian quarters burn.

title: The March on Rome
text: Mussolini's Blackshirts march on Rome and the king makes him prime minister.

title: Tutankhamun's tomb
text: Howard Carter opens the sealed tomb of Tutankhamun in the Valley of the Kings.

title: The curse of the pharaoh
text: The house reading has the tomb's guardians wake, and Lord Carnarvon's death the next spring is no accident.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Soviet Union
text: Russia, Ukraine, Belarus and Transcaucasia join as the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics.

title: The Cottingley fairies
text: The house reading has the Arcanum smile at the fairy photographs that fool Conan Doyle, and quietly visit the beck at Cottingley.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Lausanne exchange
text: Greece and Turkey trade populations; over a million Greeks and half a million Muslims are uprooted.

title: The Turkish Republic
text: Mustafa Kemal proclaims the Republic of Turkey with its capital at Ankara.

title: The Great Kanto earthquake
text: An earthquake and firestorm destroy Tokyo and Yokohama and kill over a hundred thousand; mobs murder Koreans.

title: Kanto and the Wan Kuei
text: The house reading has the Kuei-jin of Tokyo see the quake as a sign of the Sixth Age deepening.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Hyperinflation
text: The German mark collapses; a loaf of bread costs billions and the savings of the middle class vanish.

title: The beer hall putsch
text: Hitler tries to seize power in Munich and is jailed.

title: The caliphate abolished
text: The Turkish republic abolishes the caliphate and sends the last caliph into exile.

title: Lenin dies
text: Lenin dies after a series of strokes, and Stalin begins to outmanoeuvre the other heirs.

title: Kafka dies
text: Franz Kafka dies near Vienna; a friend refuses to burn the manuscripts.

title: The Menin Gate
text: The house reading has the names on the Menin Gate draw the unremembered dead of Flanders in a slow crowd.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Great Syrian Revolt
text: The Druze rise against the French, and France shells Damascus.

title: Reza Shah
text: Reza Khan ends the Qajar dynasty and crowns himself shah of Persia.

title: The May Thirtieth Movement
text: British-led police fire on protesters in Shanghai, and strikes spread across China.

title: Locarno
text: Germany, France and Belgium agree their western borders; the eastern ones are left open.

title: The Northern Expedition
text: Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists march north from Canton to beat the warlords and unify China.

title: The General Strike
text: British unions call a general strike for nine days in support of the miners.

title: The Makropulos Affair
text: Janacek's opera of a woman who has lived three hundred years opens in Brno.

title: An opera about the undying
text: The house reading has the Kindred of Brno attend Janacek's premiere and wonder who told the composer.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Shanghai massacre
text: Chiang turns on his communist allies in Shanghai and kills thousands.

title: Oil at Baba Gurgur
text: Oil gushes for days from the well at Baba Gurgur near Kirkuk, and Iraq's oil age begins.

title: Metropolis
text: Fritz Lang's film of a city of machines and workers opens in Berlin.

title: The Exhibition of Contemporary Culture
text: Brno opens its new exhibition grounds with a show of ten years of the republic; functionalist buildings rise across the city.

title: The Muslim Brotherhood
text: Hassan al-Banna, a schoolteacher, founds the Muslim Brotherhood in Ismailia to renew Egypt through Islam.

title: Penicillin
text: Alexander Fleming notices mould killing bacteria in a dish.

title: The St Wenceslas millennium
text: Czechoslovakia marks a thousand years since the murder of St Wenceslas, and St Vitus Cathedral is finished.

title: The Hebron massacre
text: Arab rioters kill sixty-seven Jews in Hebron, ending a community that had lived there for centuries.

title: The Great Crash
text: The Wall Street crash spreads ruin to Europe; two years later the Vienna Creditanstalt fails and the Depression deepens.

title: The Syndicate's crash
text: The house reading has the Syndicate allow the crash, the better to buy up the wreckage.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Villa Tugendhat
text: Mies van der Rohe finishes the Tugendhat house on a Brno hillside, a landmark of modern architecture.

title: The Salt March
text: Gandhi walks to the sea at Dandi to make salt against British law; tens of thousands are jailed.

title: The Wushe rising
text: Indigenous Seediq rise against Japanese rule in Taiwan and are crushed with gas.

title: The Mukden Incident
text: Japanese officers blow up a railway and use it to seize Manchuria.

title: The China floods
text: The Yangtze and Huai flood, and perhaps two million die.

title: Bata's Zlin
text: The shoe king Tomas Bata builds Zlin into a company town of brick and glass and sells shoes across the world.

title: The Spanish Republic
text: Spain's king leaves and a republic is proclaimed.

title: Bata dies
text: Tomas Bata dies when his plane crashes on take-off at Otrokovice.

title: The Holodomor
text: Stalin's seizure of grain and seed starves Ukraine and the Kuban; millions die in villages sealed off by police.

title: Saudi Arabia
text: Ibn Saud, master of Najd and the Hejaz, names his kingdom Saudi Arabia after his own house.

title: Iraq independent
text: Iraq joins the League of Nations as an independent kingdom.

title: Hitler chancellor
text: President Hindenburg appoints Hitler chancellor of Germany, and the Nazis take the state apart within months.

title: The Reichstag fire
text: The German parliament burns, and the Nazis use it to suspend civil rights.

title: The shadow over Germany
text: The house reading has German Kindred and Mages split over the Nazis; some see a tool, most see a fire that burns the hand.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Dachau
text: The first concentration camp opens at Dachau outside Munich, for communists, socialists and other enemies of the state.

title: Japan leaves the League
text: Japan walks out of the League of Nations over Manchuria.

title: The Austrian civil war
text: Socialist workers fight the government in Vienna for four days; the army shells the workers' flats.

title: The Night of the Long Knives
text: Hitler has the SA leaders and other rivals murdered.

title: The Long March
text: The Red Army breaks out of encirclement and marches six thousand miles to Shaanxi.

title: The Bihar earthquake
text: An earthquake on the Nepal border kills ten thousand.

title: Benes president
text: The aged Masaryk retires, and the foreign minister Edvard Benes becomes president of Czechoslovakia.

title: The Nuremberg laws
text: Germany strips Jews of citizenship and forbids marriage between Jews and other Germans.

title: The Quetta earthquake
text: An earthquake in the night destroys Quetta in Baluchistan and kills thirty thousand.

title: Persia becomes Iran
text: Reza Shah asks the world to call the country Iran.

title: The Spanish Civil War
text: Generals rise against the Spanish republic, and Europe's armies try out their weapons in Spain.

title: The Lasombra in Spain
text: The house reading has the Sabbat and the Camarilla both fight in the shadow of the Spanish war; the Lasombra claim Madrid.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Berlin Olympics
text: Germany stages the Olympics as propaganda; Jesse Owens wins four gold medals.

title: The Arab revolt in Palestine
text: Palestinian Arabs strike and rise against British rule and Jewish immigration.

title: The Xi'an Incident
text: Chiang Kai-shek is kidnapped by his own generals until he agrees to fight Japan with the communists.

title: The Masaryk circuit
text: Brno opens its road racing circuit, and the Czechoslovak Grand Prix draws crowds of a hundred thousand.

title: The war with Japan
text: Fighting at the Marco Polo Bridge begins full war between China and Japan.

title: The Nanjing massacre
text: Japanese troops kill hundreds of thousands of civilians and prisoners in Nanjing.

title: Nanjing's hungry dead
text: The house reading has the Yomi stir beneath Nanjing, and the Kuei-jin courts of the city fall.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Guernica
text: German and Italian bombers destroy the Basque town of Guernica on market day, and Picasso paints it.

title: The Great Terror
text: Stalin's police shoot hundreds of thousands and send millions to the camps.

title: The Anschluss
text: Germany annexes Austria, and Czechoslovakia is surrounded on three sides.

title: Munich
text: Britain and France agree that Germany may take the Sudetenland; Czechoslovakia is not asked.

title: The Sudetenland taken
text: German troops march into the borderlands, Opava and Znojmo among them, and Czechs flee inland.

title: Kristallnacht
text: Nazis burn synagogues and smash Jewish shops across Germany and Austria.

title: The prince goes to ground
text: The house reading has the Kindred of Brno split after Munich; some flee to Prague, the prince goes to ground under the Spilberk.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Fission
text: Hahn and Strassmann split the uranium atom in Berlin.

title: The Protectorate
text: German troops enter Prague and Brno; Bohemia and Moravia become a protectorate of the Reich and Slovakia a client state.

title: Poland invaded
text: Germany invades Poland, the Soviets follow from the east, and Britain and France declare war.

title: The universities closed
text: After student protests, Czech universities are closed, nine students are shot and twelve hundred sent to camps.

title: The Winter War
text: The Soviet Union attacks Finland, and the Finns hold in the snow for three months.

title: The coming storm
text: The house reading has the Underworld shake as the war begins; the Hierarchy prepares for the worst Maelstrom in memory.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Technocracy and the Reich
text: The house reading has the Technocracy's council forbid any convention to serve the Reich, though some Progenitors ignore it.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Katyn
text: Soviet police shoot over twenty thousand Polish officers and prisoners in the Katyn forest and elsewhere.

title: The fall of France
text: German armour breaks through the Ardennes at Sedan; France falls in six weeks.

title: Dunkirk
text: Over three hundred thousand Allied soldiers are taken off the beaches at Dunkirk.

title: The Blitz
text: German bombers attack London night after night for eight months.

title: The Blitz and the Kindred
text: The house reading has London's Kindred shelter deep in the Underground with the mortals, and Masquerade breaches go unreported in the chaos.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Czechoslovak government in exile
text: Benes forms a government in exile in London; Czechoslovak airmen fly in the Battle of Britain.

title: Japan in Indochina
text: Japanese troops enter French Indochina by agreement with Vichy, and America cuts off Japan's oil.

title: The Arcanum's blackout
text: The house reading has the Arcanum move its London library to the country and lose a crate of Prague papers on the way.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Yugoslavia invaded
text: Germany bombs Belgrade without warning and overruns Yugoslavia and Greece in a few weeks.

title: The Iraqi coup
text: A pro-Axis government in Iraq fights the British and loses; a pogrom follows in Baghdad.

title: Barbarossa
text: Germany invades the Soviet Union with three million men.

title: Iran invaded
text: Britain and the Soviets invade Iran, and Reza Shah gives up the throne to his son.

title: Babi Yar
text: German units shoot nearly thirty-four thousand Jews in two days in a ravine outside Kiev.

title: The siege of Leningrad
text: Germany surrounds Leningrad; about a million die in a siege of nearly nine hundred days.

title: Heydrich arrives
text: Reinhard Heydrich takes charge of the protectorate and begins mass arrests and executions.

title: The deportations from the protectorate
text: Jews from Prague and Brno are deported to Lodz and Terezin.

title: Hong Kong falls
text: Japan attacks Hong Kong, Malaya and Pearl Harbor in a day.

title: Moscow holds
text: The Soviets stop the Germans before Moscow in the cold and counterattack.

title: Terezin
text: The fortress town of Terezin becomes a ghetto and transit camp for the Jews of Bohemia and Moravia.

title: The children's drawings
text: The house reading has an Arcanum member smuggle out drawings from Terezin, and some of them show things no child should know.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Wannsee
text: Nazi officials meet at a villa by the Wannsee to plan the murder of Europe's Jews.

title: Singapore falls
text: Britain surrenders Singapore with eighty thousand troops, the worst defeat in its history.

title: The Heydrich attack
text: Czechoslovak paratroopers Gabcik and Kubis ambush Heydrich in a Prague street; Heydrich dies a week later.

title: Lidice
text: In revenge the Germans shoot the men of Lidice, send the women and children to camps, and raze the village.

title: Lezaky
text: The Germans destroy the hamlet of Lezaky and kill its people.

title: The church of St Cyril and Methodius
text: The paratroopers die fighting in the crypt of a Prague church.

title: The Lidice dead
text: The house reading has the dead of Lidice refuse the Hierarchy and haunt the empty fields as a Circle.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Midway
text: Japan loses four carriers at Midway in the Pacific.

title: Stalingrad
text: The Germans reach the Volga at Stalingrad, and the city becomes a battle of streets and cellars.

title: El Alamein
text: Montgomery's Eighth Army breaks Rommel's lines at El Alamein.

title: The death camps
text: The camps of Auschwitz, Treblinka, Sobibor and Belzec murder millions of Jews, Roma and others.

title: The Wyrm's harvest
text: The house reading has the Garou of Europe find the camps the deepest wounds the Wyrm has made in their age.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Bataan death march
text: Japan marches American and Filipino prisoners to camps; thousands die on the road.

title: Stalingrad surrenders
text: The frozen remnant of the German Sixth Army surrenders at Stalingrad; ninety thousand men go into captivity.

title: The Warsaw ghetto rising
text: The Jews of the Warsaw ghetto fight the Germans for a month.

title: Kursk
text: The greatest tank battle in history is fought at Kursk, and Germany loses the east.

title: The Hamburg firestorm
text: Allied bombing creates a firestorm in Hamburg that kills about forty thousand.

title: The Bengal famine
text: Famine kills perhaps three million in Bengal while rice is shipped elsewhere.

title: The Ascension War's other front
text: The house reading has the Technocracy work quietly on both the radar and the bomb, and Traditions fight to keep magic out of the war.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: D-Day
text: Allied armies land on five beaches in Normandy, and the liberation of western Europe begins.

title: The Warsaw Uprising
text: The Polish Home Army rises in Warsaw; the Soviets wait across the river while the Germans destroy the city.

title: The Slovak National Uprising
text: Slovaks rise against the Germans and their own regime; the rising is crushed in two months.

title: Brno bombed
text: Allied bombers strike Brno's factories and rail yards; hundreds of civilians die.

title: The Dukla Pass
text: Soviet and Czechoslovak troops fight their way through the Dukla Pass into Slovakia.

title: Imphal and Kohima
text: The British and Indians stop the Japanese invasion of India at Imphal and Kohima.

title: The liberation of Paris
text: The house reading has the Toreador of Paris return from hiding and quarrel over who collaborated.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Auschwitz liberated
text: Soviet troops reach Auschwitz and find seven thousand prisoners left behind by the death marches.

title: Dresden
text: Allied bombers destroy the old city of Dresden in a firestorm that kills some twenty-five thousand.

title: Yalta
text: Churchill, Roosevelt and Stalin meet at Yalta to shape postwar Europe.

title: Brno liberated
text: The Red Army takes Brno after a week of fighting.

title: The Ostrava operation
text: Soviet and Czechoslovak troops take Ostrava after weeks of fighting.

title: The Prague Uprising
text: Prague rises against the Germans; the Vlasov army changes sides and helps.

title: Germany surrenders
text: Hitler is dead in the Berlin bunker, and Germany surrenders on 8 May; Prague is still fighting.

title: The Brno death march
text: Some twenty thousand German-speaking people of Brno are driven toward the Austrian border; thousands die on the road.

title: The expulsions begin
text: Czechoslovakia begins expelling its three million Germans; many are killed in the first wild months.

title: Hiroshima and Nagasaki
text: American atomic bombs destroy Hiroshima and Nagasaki, and Japan surrenders.

title: The bomb in the Underworld
text: The house reading has the bombs tear holes in the Shroud, and the Dark Kingdom of Jade shaken to its depths.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Kuei-jin and the bomb
text: The house reading has the Kuei-jin of Japan hide from the sun the bombs made, and many never return.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Technocracy's victory
text: The house reading has the Technocracy see the bomb as proof that its paradigm has won the war.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Potsdam
text: The Allies agree how to run Germany and approve the expulsion of Germans from the east.

title: Vietnam declares independence
text: Ho Chi Minh declares an independent Vietnam in Hanoi.

title: Korea divided
text: Korea is divided at the thirty-eighth parallel between Soviet and American zones.

title: Brno's empty havens
text: The house reading has the Kindred who fled Brno return to a city of Soviet soldiers and missing German elders.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Nuremberg trials
text: The Nazi leaders are tried and many are hanged.

title: The communists win Moravia
text: The Communists come first in the free election of 1946.

title: The King David Hotel
text: Jewish militants of the Irgun bomb the British headquarters in Jerusalem's King David Hotel and kill ninety-one.

title: The Calcutta killings
text: Riots between Hindus and Muslims in Calcutta kill thousands in four days and foreshadow partition.

title: The road to Pohorelice
text: The house reading has the dead of the Brno march haunt the road south, and the Moravian Hierarchy argue about whose they are.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Partition
text: India and Pakistan become independent; millions flee and perhaps a million die.

title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
text: A Bedouin shepherd finds ancient scrolls in a cave near Qumran.

title: The scrolls watched
text: The house reading has the Celestial Chorus and the Society of Leopold both send scholars to the scrolls.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The February coup
text: The Communists take power in Czechoslovakia when the democratic ministers resign and Benes gives way.

title: Jan Masaryk falls
text: The foreign minister Jan Masaryk is found dead below his window.

title: Israel
text: Ben-Gurion declares the state of Israel in Tel Aviv, and the armies of its Arab neighbours invade.

title: The Nakba
text: Some seven hundred thousand Palestinians flee or are driven from their homes.

title: The Berlin airlift
text: The Soviets blockade West Berlin, and the Allies fly in its food for a year.

title: Gandhi killed
text: A Hindu nationalist shoots Gandhi at a prayer meeting in Delhi.

title: The People's Republic
text: Mao proclaims the People's Republic of China from the Gate of Heavenly Peace, and Chiang flees to Taiwan.

title: The Middle Kingdom falls silent
text: The house reading has the Kuei-jin courts of China driven underground by the new state.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: NATO
text: America, Canada and ten European states found the North Atlantic alliance against the Soviet bloc.

title: The Korean War
text: North Korea invades the south, and American and United Nations troops are drawn in, then China.

title: Tibet invaded
text: The Chinese army enters Tibet and defeats its small army at Chamdo.

title: The Akashics scatter
text: The house reading has the Akashic Brotherhood carry treasures out of Tibet.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Iranian oil nationalised
text: Prime Minister Mossadegh nationalises Iran's oil, and Britain blockades Iranian exports.

title: The Free Officers
text: Nasser's Free Officers overthrow King Farouk, and Egypt becomes a republic within a year.

title: The Slansky trial
text: Fourteen Communist leaders, most of them Jewish, are tried as traitors; eleven are hanged.

title: Stalin dies
text: Stalin dies at his dacha after a stroke, and the camps begin slowly to empty.

title: The Plzen rising
text: A currency reform wipes out savings, and workers in Plzen storm the town hall.

title: The coup in Iran
text: American and British agents help the army and the mobs overthrow Mossadegh, and the shah returns.

title: The Korean armistice
text: The fighting in Korea ends with the peninsula divided.

title: The Kindred in the show trials
text: The house reading has Prague's Kindred use the purges to settle their own accounts, and hunters among the secret police note odd deaths.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Dien Bien Phu
text: The Viet Minh crush the French at Dien Bien Phu.

title: The Warsaw Pact
text: The Soviet bloc forms its own military alliance in Warsaw in answer to NATO.

title: The Austrian treaty
text: The four powers leave Austria, which becomes free and neutral; Vienna is no longer divided.

title: Bandung
text: Asian and African leaders meet at Bandung in Java and found the movement of non-aligned nations.

title: Japan's new parties
text: Japan's conservatives merge into the Liberal Democratic Party, which will rule for decades.

title: The secret speech
text: Khrushchev denounces Stalin's crimes to a closed session of the party congress, and the speech leaks abroad.

title: The Hungarian revolution
text: Hungary rises against Soviet rule; Soviet tanks crush it within weeks.

title: The Suez crisis
text: Israel, Britain and France attack Egypt after Nasser takes the canal; America forces them out.

title: Polish October
text: Poland wins a gentler communism under Gomulka after riots in Poznan.

title: Blood on the Danube
text: The house reading has the Brujah of Budapest fight beside the students and the Tzimisce feed on the reprisals.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Sputnik
text: The Soviet Union puts the first satellite in orbit.

title: The Void Engineers look up
text: The house reading has the Void Engineers race to claim space for the Technocracy before the Traditions can dream it otherwise.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Kyshtym disaster
text: A nuclear waste tank explodes in the Urals and poisons a wide stretch of land; the Soviets keep it secret.

title: The Treaty of Rome
text: France, Germany, Italy and the Low Countries found the European Economic Community.

title: The Iraqi revolution
text: Officers overthrow Iraq's monarchy and kill the young king and his family in the palace courtyard.

title: The Great Leap Forward
text: Mao's Great Leap brings famine that kills tens of millions.

title: Expo 58
text: Czechoslovakia's pavilion and its Laterna Magika win the Brussels fair.

title: The Tibetan rising
text: Tibet rises against China, and the Dalai Lama flees to India.

title: The new constitution
text: Czechoslovakia declares itself a socialist republic, the second in the bloc after the Soviet Union.

title: OPEC
text: Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Venezuela found OPEC in Baghdad to take back control of oil prices.

title: Gagarin
text: Yuri Gagarin orbits the earth in Vostok 1, the first person in space.

title: The Berlin Wall
text: East Germany builds a wall through Berlin overnight to stop its people from leaving.

title: The Wall and the Kindred
text: The house reading follows canon in spirit: Berlin's Kindred divide like the city, and crossing becomes a matter for princes.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Cuban missile crisis
text: Europe waits for nuclear war for thirteen days while America and the Soviets face off over missiles in Cuba.

title: The Sino-Indian War
text: China defeats India in a short war high in the Himalayas and keeps Aksai Chin.

title: The Beatles and Glamour
text: The house reading has Liverpool's music pour Glamour into the Dreaming years before the Resurgence.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Skopje earthquake
text: An earthquake destroys most of Skopje and kills over a thousand; the city is rebuilt to a Japanese plan.

title: The Vajont dam
text: A landslide into a dam reservoir in Italy sends a wave over the dam that kills two thousand.

title: The Tokyo Olympics
text: Japan hosts the Olympics and opens the bullet train.

title: The Tonkin Gulf
text: Reports of attacks on American destroyers in the Gulf of Tonkin let America widen its war in Vietnam.

title: China's bomb
text: China tests its first atomic bomb.

title: The Indonesian killings
text: The army and militias kill half a million or more suspected communists.

title: The second Kashmir war
text: India and Pakistan fight a three-week war over Kashmir that ends where it began.

title: The Sons of Ether and the space race
text: The house reading has the Sons of Ether launch their own etherships while the Void Engineers race the Soviets.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Cultural Revolution
text: Mao unleashes the Red Guards against teachers, temples and party rivals.

title: The Red Guards and the shrines
text: The house reading has the Red Guards smash shrines the Kuei-jin had guarded for centuries; some courts are destroyed.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Florence flood
text: The Arno floods Florence, drowns its streets and damages thousands of paintings and books.

title: The Six-Day War
text: Israel takes Sinai, Gaza, the West Bank, East Jerusalem and the Golan.

title: The colonels
text: Greek colonels seize power in a coup and rule Greece for seven years.

title: The Prague Spring
text: Alexander Dubcek begins socialism with a human face, and censorship lifts.

title: The Tet Offensive
text: Communist forces attack cities across South Vietnam at the lunar new year; Hue is fought over for a month.

title: May 1968
text: Students raise barricades in Paris, millions of workers strike, and France comes to a standstill.

title: The invasion
text: Warsaw Pact troops invade Czechoslovakia; Brno's people stand in front of the tanks.

title: The Kindred and the tanks
text: The house reading has Prague's Kindred split over the Spring; Ventrue loyal to Moscow help the invaders and the Anarchs pay for it.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: My Lai
text: American soldiers kill hundreds of villagers at My Lai.

title: Hunters behind the tanks
text: The house reading has the StB open files on Brno's nightwalkers after the invasion, a knot later hunters will untangle.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Jan Palach
text: The student Jan Palach sets fire to himself in Wenceslas Square in protest.

title: The hockey riots
text: Czechoslovakia beats the Soviets twice at ice hockey, and crowds attack the Soviet airline office.

title: The Moon landing
text: Apollo 11 lands on the Moon, and the world watches on television.

title: The Resurgence
text: The house reading follows Changeling canon: the Moon landing reopens the Dreaming, and the sidhe return.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Normalisation
text: Husak's regime purges half a million party members and fires the reformers from universities, papers and theatres.

title: The Bhola cyclone
text: A cyclone kills perhaps half a million in East Pakistan.

title: Black September
text: Jordan's army fights the Palestinian guerrillas and drives them out to Lebanon.

title: Bangladesh
text: Bangladesh breaks from Pakistan after a war and mass killings.

title: The Munich massacre
text: Palestinian gunmen kill eleven Israeli athletes at the Olympics.

title: The Czech film wave
text: Many of the Czech new-wave films are banned and their makers silenced.

title: The Yom Kippur War
text: Egypt and Syria attack Israel on the holiest day of the Jewish year and are thrown back after hard fighting.

title: The oil shock
text: Arab states cut oil to the West, prices quadruple, and Europe has car-free Sundays.

title: Cyprus divided
text: Turkey invades Cyprus after a Greek-backed coup, and the island is divided by a green line.

title: Saigon falls
text: North Vietnamese tanks break into the presidential palace in Saigon; the last Americans leave by helicopter.

title: The Helsinki Accords
text: The Soviet bloc signs a promise to respect human rights.

title: The Lebanese civil war
text: Lebanon falls into fifteen years of civil war among its faiths, the Palestinians and foreign armies.

title: The Khmer Rouge
text: The Khmer Rouge empty Phnom Penh into the countryside; in four years perhaps two million Cambodians die.

title: The killing fields
text: The house reading has the Yama Kings' servants grow strong on Cambodia's dead, and the Kuei-jin of Angkor go to war against them.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Tangshan
text: An earthquake destroys Tangshan and kills a quarter of a million.

title: The Plastic People trial
text: The rock band Plastic People of the Universe is jailed.

title: Charter 77
text: Dissidents sign Charter 77 asking the state to keep its own human rights laws.

title: Kindred dissidents
text: The house reading has a few signers of Charter 77 Embraced in later years, so that some Kindred of Prague still carry the Charter's grudge.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Deng's reforms
text: Deng Xiaoping opens China's economy to markets and foreign money after Mao's death.

title: The Polish pope
text: Karol Wojtyla of Krakow becomes Pope John Paul II, the first pope from beyond Italy in four centuries.

title: The Iranian revolution
text: The shah flees, and Ayatollah Khomeini returns from exile to found an Islamic republic.

title: The Grand Mosque seized
text: Armed militants seize the Grand Mosque in Mecca and hold it for two weeks.

title: The Soviet invasion of Afghanistan
text: Soviet troops enter Afghanistan to prop up a communist government and fight a ten-year war.

title: The Garou and the mountains
text: The house reading has the Garou of the Hindu Kush fight the Soviets' shadow in the Umbra.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Solidarity
text: Shipyard workers in Gdansk strike under Lech Walesa and found Solidarity, the first free union in the bloc.

title: The Iran-Iraq War
text: Iraq invades Iran, and eight years of trench war and gas follow along the Shatt al-Arab.

title: Martial law in Poland
text: General Jaruzelski declares martial law and jails Solidarity's leaders.

title: Sadat killed
text: Soldiers shoot President Sadat at a military parade.

title: Sabra and Shatila
text: Lebanese militias kill hundreds of Palestinians in the Sabra and Shatila camps while Israeli troops ring them.

title: Hama
text: Syria crushes a rising in Hama and kills thousands.

title: The Beirut barracks
text: Truck bombs kill American and French peacekeepers in Beirut.

title: Bhopal
text: A gas leak from a pesticide plant kills thousands.

title: The Golden Temple
text: Indian troops storm the Golden Temple, and Indira Gandhi is killed by bodyguards.

title: Gorbachev
text: Mikhail Gorbachev takes power and begins glasnost and perestroika.

title: Chernobyl
text: A reactor explodes at Chernobyl and spreads fallout across Europe.

title: The Wyrm at Chernobyl
text: The house reading follows Werewolf canon in spirit: the Black Spiral Dancers claim the poisoned zone.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Technocracy covers Chernobyl
text: The house reading has the New World Order help the Soviets hide the scale of the disaster.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The first intifada
text: Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank rise against Israeli occupation.

title: Halabja
text: Iraq attacks the Kurdish town of Halabja with poison gas and kills thousands.

title: The Spitak earthquake
text: An earthquake in northern Armenia kills twenty-five thousand and levels Spitak.

title: Lockerbie
text: A bomb destroys an airliner over Lockerbie in Scotland.

title: Tiananmen
text: The army clears Tiananmen Square of protesters and kills hundreds or more.

title: The Wall falls
text: A muddled announcement opens the border, and East Germans pour through the Berlin Wall.

title: The Velvet Revolution
text: Students beaten in Prague start the Velvet Revolution, and the communists give way within weeks.

title: Brno's Velvet days
text: Crowds fill Freedom Square in Brno as the regime collapses.

title: The Romanian revolution
text: Romania rises against Ceausescu, who is caught, tried in an hour and shot on Christmas Day.

title: Havel president
text: The playwright Vaclav Havel, jailed a year before, is elected president by the old parliament.

title: The Kindred after the fall
text: The house reading has the Camarilla rush into the old bloc as the Sabbat and the old bloc's princes scramble.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The velvet Dreaming
text: The house reading has the Velvet Revolution light the Dreaming of Prague, and the Kithain of Brno dance on Freedom Square.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Red Summer
text: White mobs attack black neighbourhoods in some two dozen American cities; in Chicago and Washington the residents fight back.

title: Prohibition
text: The making and sale of alcohol is forbidden across the United States, and a generation of gangsters gets rich.

title: Tulsa
text: A white mob burns the prosperous black district of Greenwood and kills perhaps three hundred.

title: The great Mississippi flood
text: The river breaks its levees from Illinois to the Gulf and drives hundreds of thousands from their homes, many of them north for good.

title: Vargas takes Brazil
text: An armed revolt puts Getulio Vargas in power for fifteen years.

title: The Chaco War
text: Bolivia and Paraguay fight three years for a thorn wilderness wrongly believed to hold oil.

title: Black Sunday
text: A wall of dust turns day to night on the southern plains; farm families by the hundred thousand take the road west.

title: The Parsley massacre
text: Trujillo's soldiers kill thousands of Haitians along the Dominican border in under a week.

title: Mexico takes its oil
text: President Cardenas expropriates the foreign oil companies.

title: The camps
text: More than a hundred thousand Japanese Americans and Japanese Canadians are removed from the Pacific coast to inland camps.

title: Trinity
text: The first atomic bomb is set off in the New Mexico desert.

title: Peron
text: Juan Peron is elected president of Argentina with the votes of the unions.

title: The Bogotazo
text: The murder of a popular leader sets Bogota on fire and opens ten years of killing in the countryside.

title: The coup in Guatemala
text: An invasion arranged by American intelligence overthrows a president who had taken idle land from a fruit company.

title: Separate is not equal
text: The Supreme Court rules that segregated public schools are unlawful.

title: The bus boycott
text: Rosa Parks keeps a seat, and the black citizens of Montgomery walk to work for a year.

title: The Cuban Revolution
text: The dictator flies out on New Year's Day, and Fidel Castro's rebels enter Havana a week later.

title: The Valdivia earthquake
text: The strongest earthquake ever measured strikes southern Chile, and its wave kills people in Hawaii and Japan.

title: Brasilia
text: Brazil moves its capital to a new city built in four years on the empty plateau.

title: The Bay of Pigs
text: Cuban exiles trained by American intelligence land in Cuba and are beaten in three days.

title: The missiles in Cuba
text: American aircraft photograph Soviet missiles in Cuba, and for thirteen days the navies face each other at a quarantine line.

title: Kennedy shot
text: The American president is shot dead in an open car in Dallas, three months after a quarter of a million people marched on Washington for civil rights.

title: The generals take Brazil
text: A coup begins twenty-one years of military rule.

title: Guevara shot
text: Bolivian soldiers with American advisers capture Che Guevara and shoot him.

title: King shot
text: Martin Luther King is shot dead in Memphis, and more than a hundred American cities burn.

title: Tlatelolco
text: Soldiers fire on a student meeting in the Plaza of the Three Cultures ten days before the Olympic Games open.

title: Stonewall
text: The patrons of a Greenwich Village bar fight back against a police raid for several nights.

title: The Moon
text: Two men from a ship launched in Florida walk on the Moon.

title: The Ancash earthquake
text: An earthquake shakes loose part of a glacier in Peru, and the town of Yungay is buried with nearly everyone in it.

title: Wounded Knee occupied
text: Oglala Lakota and the American Indian Movement hold the village of Wounded Knee against federal marshals for seventy-one days.

title: The coup in Chile
text: The armed forces bomb the presidential palace; President Allende dies inside, and thousands are tortured or disappear.

title: The dirty war
text: A junta takes Argentina and makes some thirty thousand people disappear; their mothers begin to walk each week in the Plaza de Mayo.

title: Jonestown
text: More than nine hundred members of an American church die by poison at their settlement in Guyana.

title: The Sandinistas
text: Rebels overthrow the Somoza dynasty in Nicaragua, and a decade of war with American-backed forces follows.

title: Romero shot
text: The archbishop of San Salvador is shot at the altar a day after telling soldiers to stop the repression.

title: Mount St. Helens
text: The north face of the volcano slides away and the blast flattens the forest for miles.

title: The Shining Path
text: A Maoist party in the Peruvian highlands burns ballot boxes on election eve and begins a war that kills some seventy thousand.

title: The Falklands war
text: Argentina's junta seizes the islands, Britain retakes them in ten weeks, and the junta falls the next year.

title: The Mexico City earthquake
text: An earthquake brings down hundreds of buildings in the capital; neighbours dig out the living while the state hesitates.

title: Armero
text: Mud from the eruption of Nevado del Ruiz buries the Colombian town of Armero and more than twenty thousand people.

title: The Caracazo
text: Price rises set off riots in Caracas, and the army kills hundreds, perhaps thousands.

title: Panama invaded
text: American troops invade Panama to seize its ruler.

title: Annual
text: The Rif fighters of Abd el-Krim destroy a Spanish army in northern Morocco.

title: The Women's War
text: Tens of thousands of Igbo and Ibibio women rise against the warrant chiefs and a rumoured tax; troops shoot more than fifty.

title: Haile Selassie crowned
text: Ras Tafari is crowned emperor of Ethiopia; in Jamaica some see the event as prophecy fulfilled.

title: Italy invades Ethiopia
text: Italian armies invade with aircraft and poison gas, and the emperor pleads in vain before the League of Nations.

title: The emperor returns
text: British, African and Ethiopian forces drive out the Italians, and Haile Selassie re-enters the capital five years to the day after it fell.

title: Thiaroye
text: French troops shoot West African soldiers, freed prisoners of war, who were demanding their back pay near Dakar.

title: Setif
text: A victory parade in Algeria turns into a rising, and the reprisals kill thousands.

title: The Malagasy rising
text: A revolt against French rule is crushed over two years at a cost of tens of thousands of lives.

title: Apartheid
text: The National Party wins South Africa's whites-only election and begins to write separation into law.

title: The emergency in Kenya
text: Britain declares an emergency against the Mau Mau and holds more than a hundred thousand Kikuyu in camps.

title: The Algerian war
text: The National Liberation Front opens a war for independence with attacks across Algeria on All Saints' Day.

title: Ghana
text: The Gold Coast becomes independent as Ghana under Kwame Nkrumah.

title: Guinea says no
text: Guinea alone votes against de Gaulle's French community; the French leave at once and take even the light bulbs.

title: Sharpeville
text: South African police fire on a crowd protesting the pass laws and kill sixty-nine.

title: The year of Africa
text: Seventeen African states become independent; the Congo's army mutinies within a week and its richest province breaks away.

title: Lumumba killed
text: The Congo's deposed first prime minister is handed to his enemies in Katanga and shot.

title: Algeria independent
text: After eight years of war Algeria is independent, and nearly a million settlers leave within months.

title: The Organisation of African Unity
text: Thirty-two states found a union in Addis Ababa and agree to keep the colonial borders.

title: The Zanzibar revolution
text: A rising overthrows the sultan a month after independence, and thousands of Arabs and Indians are killed.

title: The Rivonia trial
text: Nelson Mandela and seven others are sentenced to prison for life.

title: Rhodesia breaks away
text: The white government of Rhodesia declares independence rather than accept majority rule.

title: Nkrumah overthrown
text: The army takes power in Ghana while the president is abroad, weeks after the first of Nigeria's coups.

title: Biafra
text: Eastern Nigeria secedes as Biafra after massacres of Igbo in the north; war and blockade kill more than a million in thirty months.

title: Amin
text: Idi Amin takes power in Uganda; some three hundred thousand are killed in eight years, and the Asians are expelled.

title: The emperor deposed
text: Soldiers depose Haile Selassie after a hidden famine, and the Derg rules by terror.

title: Portugal's empire ends
text: Angola and Mozambique become independent, and both go straight into civil war.

title: Soweto
text: Police fire on schoolchildren marching against lessons in Afrikaans, and the townships rise.

title: Biko
text: Steve Biko dies of head injuries in police custody.

title: Zimbabwe
text: After a long bush war Rhodesia becomes Zimbabwe under Robert Mugabe.

title: The Ethiopian famine
text: Drought and war starve the Ethiopian highlands; a television report from Korem moves the world, and perhaps a million die.

title: Lake Nyos
text: A crater lake in Cameroon releases a cloud of carbon dioxide in the night and suffocates seventeen hundred people.

title: Sankara killed
text: The young revolutionary president of Burkina Faso is shot in a coup led by a close comrade.

title: Coniston
text: A police party in central Australia kills at least thirty-one Warlpiri, Anmatyerre and Kaytetye people; an inquiry clears it.

title: Black Saturday in Apia
text: New Zealand police fire on a peaceful march of the Samoan independence movement and kill a high chief and ten others.

title: The Hawke's Bay earthquake
text: An earthquake and fire destroy Napier and Hastings; Napier is rebuilt in the style of the day.

title: The harbour bridge
text: The Sydney Harbour Bridge opens in the depth of the depression.

title: Pearl Harbor
text: Japanese carrier aircraft sink much of the American Pacific fleet at its moorings in Hawaii.

title: Darwin bombed
text: The carriers that struck Pearl Harbor bomb Darwin, the first of about a hundred raids on northern Australia.

title: The Kokoda track
text: Australian militia and Papuan carriers stop a Japanese army in the mountains within sight of Port Moresby.

title: Guadalcanal
text: American marines land in the Solomon Islands and hold an airfield through six months of fighting.

title: The tests at Bikini
text: The people of Bikini are moved away so that atomic bombs can be tested on their atoll; they are still waiting to go home.

title: Castle Bravo
text: A hydrogen bomb far stronger than planned drops fallout on Rongelap and on a Japanese fishing boat.

title: Maralinga
text: Britain tests atomic bombs on Anangu land in South Australia.

title: The Antarctic Treaty
text: Twelve states agree to keep Antarctica for science and to freeze their claims.

title: Samoa independent
text: Western Samoa is the first Pacific island state to regain independence.

title: The referendum
text: Nine in ten Australians vote to count Aboriginal people in the census and let the Commonwealth make laws for them.

title: Cyclone Tracy
text: A cyclone flattens Darwin on Christmas morning.

title: Papua New Guinea
text: Papua New Guinea becomes independent of Australia.

title: The land march
text: Whina Cooper, nearly eighty, leads a Maori march the length of the North Island under the words not one more acre.

title: Erebus
text: A sightseeing airliner from Auckland flies into Mount Erebus in Antarctica with the loss of all 257 aboard.

title: The Rainbow Warrior
text: French agents sink a protest ship in Auckland harbour and kill a photographer.

title: Uluru handed back
text: The title to Uluru is returned to the Anangu, who lease it back as a park.

title: The coups in Fiji
text: A colonel twice seizes power in Fiji in the name of the indigenous Fijians.

title: Bougainville
text: Landowners sabotage a giant copper mine, and ten years of war and blockade follow.

title: Black January
text: Soviet troops storm Baku after pogroms against Armenians and kill over a hundred civilians.

title: Lithuania breaks away
text: Lithuania declares independence from the Soviet Union, the first republic to do so.

title: The hyphen war
text: Czechs and Slovaks quarrel over the country's new name and settle on the Czech and Slovak Federative Republic.

title: The first free election
text: Czechoslovakia's first free election in forty-four years gives Civic Forum a landslide; Moravian regional parties win seats.

title: The Manjil earthquake
text: An earthquake in northern Iran kills over thirty-five thousand.

title: Iraq invades Kuwait
text: Saddam Hussein's army overruns Kuwait in a day.

title: German reunification
text: East Germany joins the Federal Republic, and Germany is one state again.

title: The tourists come
text: Western tourists flood Prague, and the old town fills with exchange booths and beer.

title: The Camarilla comes east

text: The house reading follows the approved timeline: faith flows to the Fallen so freely that some remember why they fell, and others grow worse.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The crusade wins Prague
text: A crusader coalition wins the Czech election on a promise of purge law, and the gates go up in Prague's stations within a month.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The thinning walls
text: Hamburg's people see the dead in the streets after dark, and the city stops pretending it does not.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: Brno's gates
text: Thermal gates go up in Brno's stations a month after Prague's, and the Brno Elysium goes dark.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The Rothenstein trials
text: The crusade reaches Moravia, and Rothenstein's old families are tried in public for hiding Kindred for centuries.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The flight from Brno
text: Brno's revealed and those who sheltered them flee south to Vienna, east to the glass and north into the mountains.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The old families' price
text: The house reading has the elders the old families hid let them hang to keep their own havens secret, and the families' heirs never forgive them.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Merciful of Olomouc
text: The house reading has Merciful imbued in Olomouc smuggle Rothenstein's children out before the trials end.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Thin-blood alchemy
text: Thin-blood alchemy is sold on Berlin's streets like any drug, and the purge states cannot stop it at the border.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: China on Mars
text: A Chinese colony ship lands on Mars beside the old Euro-Soviet base.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: District reality
text: Tokyo's arcologies find that warding charms sold to tenants work in one tower and fail in the next.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: Venice drowned
text: The sea barrier at Venice fails for good, and the restored city is left to the tides; its owners move the festivals to the Alps.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: Hamburg's caerns dark
text: The last spirit places inside Hamburg go dark, and the city's Garou take Weaver patrons or leave.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The heat wall
text: Summer heat in the Gulf passes what people can survive outdoors, and the charter cities seal their streets under glass.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The suicide virus
text: A program loose on a Seoul corporate grid drives hundreds of workers to suicide in one night; Netwatch blames a rival, and no one believes it.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: Spectres in the code
text: The house reading follows the approved timeline: the virus is Spectral, and Seoul's dead are its first victims.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The shifters' Concord
text: Shapechangers who hid for centuries meet on the glass and swear a new Concord with the Garou of the waste septs.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The Accord comes to Tokyo
text: Japan adopts the Night City Accord, and registered Kindred, Garou and imbued sign it as a condition of their contracts.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: Vienna's refugees
text: Vienna takes in Moravian refugees and gives them papers that do not ask about pulses.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The school attacked
text: Gunmen strike the Alexandria school and kill teachers and students; the attackers are found dead in the desert a week later.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: Set's answer
text: The house reading follows the approved timeline: Set's followers strike the school and every adviser they can find, and the mummies prepare their reply.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The teachers' followers
text: Millions across Asia follow the Taipei teachers' lessons in balance, and the old courts call them traitors.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The Russian core falls
text: Moscow's government collapses into rival corporate fiefs, and Russia is ruled from company towns.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The elders' ceasefire
text: The corps buy peace from the elders the crusade could not reach, in exchange for what the old blood knows; the young call it betrayal.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: Chi for sale
text: Wan Kuei in Neo-Kowloon sell chi to the corps and to Western Kindred, and the old courts call it selling the Dragon.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The Brno rising
text: Brno's workers rise against the crusader government; the army retakes the city in three days.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The Lyon heresy
text: Lyon's people break with the crusade and declare a free commune; the crusade surrounds it.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: Voices under the glass
text: Cults on the glass hear voices calling from beneath it, and pilgrims dig.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The Earthbound call
text: The house reading follows the approved timeline: the Earthbound beneath the glass begin calling their old servants home.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Delhi's walls
text: Delhi walls itself against the delta refugees and becomes a city of eighty million.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The dead come back
text: In Hamburg the dead begin returning to their own bodies in the morgues, and the city's undertakers hire armed guards.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The vault city
text: Ostrava's old mine shafts become a city of data vaults, run by a firm no one has seen.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The registry bought
text: Japan's registry is bought, share by share, by its oldest members, and the list of every haven is sold to the highest bidder.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The Spanish dust
text: Southern Spain turns to dust, and its people move north into France and the Alps.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The Nile fails
text: The Nile runs low for three years, and Cairo's people turn to the mummies for help.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The born imbued
text: Children born to imbued parents in the Lyon commune see what others cannot from their first year.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The arcology wars
text: China's arcologies fight open wars for water and power through hired armies.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The Moravian dust bowl
text: South Moravia's fields turn to dust, and Mikulov's last farmers sell to a water firm.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The Vienna Concord
text: Vienna hosts a meeting of every line, and they agree on almost nothing but meeting again.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The citadel in the Shadowlands
text: Rothenstein's people see the dead manning the walls at night, and the crusade's priests refuse to go near.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The Gulf's end
text: The last Gulf oil field closes, and the charter cities live on finance and water rights.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The clinic fires
text: Free clinics burn on one night in Marseille, Cairo, Istanbul and Delhi.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The Earthbound strike
text: The house reading follows the approved timeline: the clinics belonged to the Reconcilers, and the Earthbound burned them.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Brno's long decline
text: Brno is half empty, its data vaults sold, its trade fair a market for scrap and stolen chrome.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The heresy courts
text: With few monsters left to try, the crusade's courts start calling ordinary dissenters heretics.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: Moravia holds
text: The house reading follows the approved timeline: the Hierarchy's legions break everywhere but Moravia.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Seoul vote
text: Korea's voters are asked whether magic is real; the result is a tie.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The dream market bottled
text: Tokyo's corporations bottle dreams and sell them, and the street dream markets close.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The Hamburg dead count
text: Hamburg's census counts more ghosts than living in some districts.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: Spirits in the walls
text: Glass Walkers on arcology security find wild spirits sealed in Hamburg's walls, still calling.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The Accord murders
text: A string of murders in Lyon, Tokyo and Seoul breaks the Accord in three cities at once.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The deep glass stirs
text: Things climb out of the deep glass at the Meltdown's heart, and the waste septs fall back.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The Duat darkens
text: The Alexandria school's priests report that the Underworld darkens at its western edge.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: Stories in the wastes
text: Wandering storytellers in the southern wastes keep the old tales alive for children no one else visits.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: Heralds in the markets
text: Strangers walk the night markets of Neo-Kowloon and the Kuei-jin flee them.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The Demon Emperor's heralds
text: The house reading follows the approved timeline: the heralds are the Demon Emperor's, and the Sixth Age is at its height.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The last nest
text: Three Kuei-jin courts and a corporate army fight over the last untapped nest in Asia.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The Reconcilers pray
text: In Vienna a circle of the Fallen prays in a ruined church, and the city hears singing at midnight.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: Holes in the wall
text: Projectors map the wall between life and death and find holes the size of cities, Hamburg the largest.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The Hungry Dead
text: Starving Kuei-jin lose themselves, and Hungry Dead hunt Tokyo's arcologies by night.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The empty cities
text: The crusade's cities are nearly empty of the revealed; the wastes are full of them.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The crusade belt
text: The crusade rules a belt of cities from Rome to Hamburg, and its inquisitors whisper that its leaders cast no reflection.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: Brno's wards
text: The last people of Brno ward their doors with salt and iron.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: Apophis turns
text: The mummies of Cairo dream of the serpent Apophis turning in its sleep.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The last night of Rothenstein
text: Rothenstein's walls are full of the dead, and its people wait for the end.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading

title: The last Concord
text: The lines meet in Vienna one last time and choose their sides for the Time of Future Judgement.
ref: Future Darkness branch history, a house reading
